#77166. Sexual harassment overhaul at a crossroads in the House

Sexual harassment overhaul at a crossroads in the House

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va.
  • The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.
  • Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, said legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.

It has been revealed that rep. Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, said legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.

It has been revealed that “Yes, absolutely,” she said when asked if the package would get a vote this year. “We’re shopping it now with the different committees, House Admin and Ethics, and waiting on their final feedback, which we should have actually this week.”.

Industry observers note that rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, said she was still optimistic about getting it done, but stopped short of putting full faith in Republican leadership to get it over the finish line. The effort has been underway since May, when Cammack and Leger Fernández’s caucuses declared a partnership to propose changes after two members of the House resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct.

Asked if she thought Speaker Mike Johnson would put the proposal on the floor during the busy lame-duck session, Leger Fernández laughed.

“Hopefully, that’s something that will happen, because you know the Republican Women’s Caucus had remarked they were optimistic before we left. I’m still optimistic,” she said.

It has been revealed that the two groups have spent months holding dozens of meetings with staff, their own caucuses and male members of Congress, among others. Suggestions have included banning members of Congress from engaging in sexual relationships with any House staffer, not just those who work for them directly, and outlining penalties for violaters. Initially, the groups were expected to unveil their work by August recess, but that got pushed back as the House canceled weeks in session and as they cited a desire to get it right.

Cammack said she thinks Johnson “has been very sincere in his efforts on this.”.

In a recent development, “That would be a tremendous disappointment” if he didn’t put it on the floor, she said when asked about the possibility. “I genuinely believe he cares about this glitch.”.

It has been revealed that leger Fernández said if it doesn’t get done by the end of the 119th Congress, she hopes some changes would be adopted under the rules package for the next Congress that Democrats bring forward in January. Such packages are typically adopted with party-line votes and give incoming majorities the chance to tweak how the House operates to their liking. While certain narrower proposals aimed at curbing sexual harassment could be written into House rules, others would need to pass both chambers and be enacted into law to take effect.

“We are going to move to make sure it is in the rules package, because we will be in charge next year,” Leger Fernández said. “But I would love for it to pass now, because that was a commitment that it be bipartisan.”.

#77165. 12 Airline Booking Traps That Could Cost You Money in 2026

12 Airline Booking Traps That Could Cost You Money in 2026

📅 19 Jun 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Airline websites are not necessarily badly designed, even though they often feel that way.
  • It has been revealed that you start with a flight that looks like it costs $400.
  • Industry observers note that after more than 18 years of travel to over 130 countries, we still catch ourselves slowing down to double-check airline bookings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Airline websites are not necessarily badly designed, even though they often feel that way. In many cases, the booking process is doing exactly what it was designed to do: get you focused on the lowest advertised fare before revealing the cost of everything else.

It has been revealed that you start with a flight that looks like it costs $400. By the time you add a carry-on bag, choose a seat, and work through the final checkout screens, the total is suddenly $650.

Industry observers note that after more than 18 years of travel to over 130 countries, we still catch ourselves slowing down to double-check airline bookings. The difference now is that we know where the expensive mistakes are usually hiding. We also use flight-search and tracking tools to compare routes and monitor changes. See our guide to the best travel apps for 2026.

The lowest price on the first screen is rarely enough information to tell you which flight is actually cheapest. You need to compare the complete journey, including baggage, seats, fare restrictions, connections, operating airlines, and the risk involved if something goes wrong.

In a recent development, to avoid costly airline booking mistakes, compare the total price of the journey rather than the advertised base fare. Check the conditions of the exact fare, baggage allowances, operating airline, cabin on every segment, connection times, and whether the flights are issued on one protected ticket.Before paying, compare the flight as a round trip, two one-way tickets, and a multi-city itinerary. Before leaving home, verify your passport, visas or travel authorizations, transit requirements, check-in deadline, and gate-closing time.

These airline booking traps—also common flight-booking mistakes—can turn an apparently cheap ticket into the most expensive option.

One of the first mistakes travellers make is comparing flights by airline logo.

You see the airline you normally use, remember the points sitting in your account, and stop comparing. But loyalty should not convince you to pay hundreds of dollars more for a worse schedule, a more restrictive ticket, or a fare that excludes everything you need.

In a recent development, airline points can still be valuable, especially when you are close to earning useful status or have benefits such as complimentary baggage. But loyalty should be one part of the calculation, not the starting point.

Before choosing an airline, compare:.

In a recent development, the days of automatically paying more because “this is our airline” are over. Loyalty should follow value, not the other way around.

Basic Economy can be a perfectly reasonable fare. The trap is buying it without understanding what has been removed.

It may work well when you are taking a short flight, travelling with only a small personal item, do not care where you sit, and are confident your intends will not change.

The problem is that airline websites normally display the lowest available fare first. Once you are in booking mode, it is easy to select that number and move forward without reading the restrictions.

You may save $40 on the ticket and then spend $85 adding the carry-on bag you needed from the beginning.

Before booking Basic Economy, price the next fare category. A Standard Economy ticket may cost more initially but include a carry-on bag, checked luggage, seat selection, or greater flexibility.

According to recent reports, also consider whether seat selection genuinely matters. Travellers with children, mobility considerations, medical needs, or a strong need for an aisle or window seat should include that cost when comparing fares.

Do not buy the lowest number. Buy the fare that includes what you actually need.

Airlines do not necessarily sell every Economy Class seat at the same price. Seats are divided into fare classes or pricing tiers, often called fare buckets.

When the cheapest tier sells out, the price can jump even when the aircraft still has many empty seats.

It has been revealed that that is one reason a flight might appear at $480 in the morning and $620 later that day. It does not always mean the plane suddenly filled up. It may mean the least expensive fare class is no longer available.

When you see a noticeable price increase, do not assume you must either pay it immediately or lose the trip.

Start the comparison again and check:.

Industry observers note that A competitor may now be cheaper. In other cases, the next fare level may include baggage, seat selection, or flexibility that makes it better value than the stripped-down ticket you were originally considering. A fare jump is a signal to widen the search, not automatically accept the latest price.

For the tools we use to compare dates, airports, and fare changes, see our guide to the best travel apps for finding flights.

The standard airline search box encourages travellers to enter a departure city, destination, outbound date, and return date.

That does not mean a traditional round trip is always the cheapest or most efficient way to book.

Before purchasing an expensive international itinerary, compare it three ways:.

An open-jaw ticket means flying into one city and returning home from another.

For example, if you are travelling through Europe, you might fly into Paris and return from Rome. Even if the airfare is similar to a return ticket from Paris, you could avoid paying for a train or flight back to your starting point. You may also save a hotel night and an entire day of backtracking.

Different airlines can also be used in each direction. One carrier may offer the best outbound flight, while another has a much better return schedule.

When comparing separate tickets, check baggage fees, fare restrictions, connection risks, and cancellation policies. The goal is not to find the cleverest itinerary. It is to determine which option gives you the best total trip.

With a codeshare flight, the airline selling the ticket may not be the airline flying the plane.

You might purchase the journey through one airline’s website and then arrive at the airport to discover that a partner carrier operates the flight.

Before buying, look for the words “operated by” in the flight details.

According to recent reports, then check the itinerary on both airline websites. Confirm the aircraft, seat map, baggage allowance, terminal, and check-in instructions.

After booking, make sure you have the operating carrier’s reservation number. The confirmation number issued by the airline selling the ticket may not work on the partner airline’s website.

Codeshares are not automatically bad. They can provide more destinations and useful connections. The problem is that they create a handoff between companies, and that handoff can become confusing when you need assistance.

As we have learned, one of the most expensive sentences in travel can be: “You need to contact the other airline.”.

Mixed-cabin fares are one of the easiest airline traps to miss.

The search result may display a large Premium Economy or Business Class label, making it appear that the entire journey is in the upgraded cabin.

Then you expand the flight details and discover that the 40-minute connection is in Premium Economy while the eight-hour overnight flight is in regular Economy.

We have come close to booking this type of itinerary several times.

Before paying, check the cabin listed beside every individual segment. Make sure the premium seat is on the flight where you will actually benefit from it.

Do not assume one premium segment provides premium benefits throughout the trip.

Sources indicate that screenshot the cabin shown for each flight and confirm that it appears correctly in the final reservation. A mixed-cabin fare is only a deal when the upgraded cabin is on the part of the journey that matters.

There is rarely one simple baggage policy that applies to every passenger flying with an airline.

Sources indicate that do not check only the airline’s general baggage page. Open the conditions attached to the specific fare and route you are considering.

Sources indicate that this is especially vital when connecting from a transatlantic flight to a smaller airline or low-cost carrier within Europe. A bag accepted on the first flight may be too large, too heavy, or not included on the next one.

A bag fitting inside the overhead compartment does not automatically mean it meets the airline’s rules. Wheels, handles, and outside pockets are normally included when the bag is measured.

Recent findings suggest that price your luggage before buying the flight. A ticket that appears $30 cheaper can rapidly become more expensive once the necessary baggage is added.

Paying for bags online in advance is also frequently less expensive than waiting until the airport, although the difference varies by airline.

Finally, weigh your suitcase at home using a real scale. Picking it up and declaring that it “feels about 20 kilos” is not a reliable baggage strategy.

Once you know your allowance, follow our two-minute checked-bag routine before handing your suitcase over at the airport.

A self-transfer may be the most expensive mistake in this guide.

Recent findings suggest that some search and booking sites combine two separate tickets and display them as one journey. Look for warnings such as:.

The critical detail is that the airlines may not recognize the flights as one protected itinerary.

If the first flight is delayed and you miss the second one, the second airline may consider you a no-show. You could lose the remaining flights on that reservation and be forced to purchase a newly introduced last-minute ticket.

The first airline may not be responsible for helping because it transported you to the destination shown on its ticket.

A self-transfer can also require you to:.

Leaving the international transit area can also trigger entry or transit requirements that would not apply during a normal airside connection.

Self-transfers can work when you have a long buffer, carry-on luggage, an airport you understand, and enough flexibility to absorb a disruption.

We would not use one when connecting to a cruise, wedding, organized tour, or once-daily long-haul flight.

Always compare the self-transfer price with a protected itinerary. The higher fare may not simply be buying convenience. It may be buying the airline’s responsibility to get you to your final destination.

Airlines can sell a connection that technically meets the airport’s minimum requirements.

That does not necessarily mean it is comfortable, sensible, or suitable for you.

A 45-minute connection at a large international airport might involve:.

If a connection makes you nervous while sitting at home, it will not feel better when you are waiting for the aircraft door to open. Choose connection time based on the consequences of missing the next flight.

According to recent reports, A long layover can be inconvenient. A missed connection can cost a full day or derail the entire trip.

Recent findings suggest that we use third-party flight sites for research. They are useful for comparing airlines, dates, and routing options.

Buying through one is a separate decision.

Sources indicate that A third-party fare may be genuinely cheaper, but make sure you are comparing the same product. It could involve:.

The biggest problem normally appears when the schedule changes or the flight is cancelled.

It has been revealed that the airline may tell you to contact the company that issued the ticket. The booking company may then tell you that only the airline can resolve the flight.

Before buying, find the itinerary through the search site and compare it directly with the airline. When the price difference is small, booking with the airline may be worth it for easier communication during disruptions.

Also check the payment currency. Some booking sites offer to convert the total into your home currency. This feels convenient but may include a less favourable exchange rate.

Sources indicate that when your credit card does not charge a foreign transaction fee, paying in the original currency may be less expensive. Compare the final converted amount and check your card’s fees rather than choosing a currency based on familiarity.

Some of the most expensive travel problems do not happen during booking. They happen at the airport after your hotel, tour, rental car, or cruise has already been paid for.

A valid passport may not be enough to enter your destination or transit through a connecting country.

Depending on your nationality, route, and destination, you may need:.

A passport can be valid on your departure date and still fail to meet the destination’s entry requirements. Complicated connections are also a good reason to review our international travel safety tips before departure.

Recent findings suggest that names matter too. The name on your airline ticket should match your passport and any visa or travel authorization. Do not assume that a nickname or commonly used name will be accepted.

Before an international trip, take five minutes to verify:.

Canadian travellers should verify current destination-specific requirements using official government travel advisories and the relevant embassy or immigration authority, since entry and transit rules can change.

It has been revealed that five minutes at home can save the entire trip at the airport. For our complete pre-departure routine, read our travel safety checklist for 2026.

In a recent development, departure time is when the aircraft is scheduled to leave. It is not the time you should arrive at the gate.

Boarding begins earlier, and the gate closes before departure. The exact cutoff depends on the airport, airline, route, and destination.

Once the gate is closed, seeing the aircraft through the terminal window will not save your seat.

Sources indicate that if you miss the flight, the cost may extend far beyond a replacement ticket. You might also lose:.

Build your airport schedule backward from the airline’s check-in, baggage-drop, boarding, and gate-closing deadlines.

Recent findings suggest that check current security conditions using the airport’s official app or website, but do not treat an estimated wait time as a guarantee. Add time for airport parking, shuttle transportation, baggage drop, security, passport control, terminal changes, and finding the gate.

According to recent reports, it is better to have extra time near the gate than to spend the start of your trip running through an airport while your name is being called over the loudspeaker. Arriving early does not help much if your carry-on slows you down at screening. Read our airport security tips and common mistakes before packing.

Before confirming a flight, we recommend checking the entire itinerary one final time.

It has been revealed that the best defence against airline booking traps is not a secret search setting or complicated flight hack. It is slowing down long enough to compare the complete journey.

All 12 of these traps work best when travellers are rushing.

We see a low fare, get excited about the trip, and want to finish before the number changes. The booking process then reveals the bags, seats, restrictions, connections, and other costs after we have already become emotionally committed to the flight.

Recent findings suggest that the cheapest flight is not necessarily the one with the lowest number on the first screen. It is the flight that gets you to your destination without surprise charges, unrealistic connections, or an expensive problem at the airport.

After more than 18 years of travelling, experience has not made us immune to booking mistakes. It has simply taught us when to stop, reopen the details, and check everything one more time.

Take five minutes before pressing confirm. Those five minutes could save hundreds of dollars—or save the entire trip.

How I Got My Visa to France

📅 16 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010.
  • But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées.
  • Industry observers note that since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been in love with France ever since my first trip to Bordeaux in 2010. Friends I had met back in Thailand demonstrated me around the area and introduced me to French culture. It was my first time in France and I loved the food, the wine, and the people.

But that love became an obsession when, after Bordeaux, I stepped out of the Paris metro and onto the Champs-Élysées. The lights, the energy, the mystique! There was magic in the air. I felt like I had known the city my entire life and I was simply returning home.

Industry observers note that since then, Paris has had a firm grip on my heart. Over the years, I spent countless visits exploring France and Paris in particular. I’ve run tours in the city and I spent a few months living there in 2019.

Last August, after yet another sojourn, I thought to myself, “What if I moved back?”.

Sources indicate that I was growing a bit tired of the NYC dating scene, the rising cost of living, and felt like, creatively, I was in a rut. With AI coming for creators like me and the industry changing, I was a little lost on what, career-wise, would come next.

And Paris seemed like the best place to go.

It’s cheaper than NYC, I had friends there already, I’ve always wanted to learn French, it would make a great base for exploring Europe, and I could start writing my next book there. There’s nothing like a change in scenery to get the creativity flowing!

But the question remained: how do you move to France?

After all, they don’t have a digital nomad visa, and you’re limited to three months if you visit on your regular Schengen tourist visa.

Well, it turns out that it’s not actually that hard. (And while I can only speak for Americans, I suspect the criteria are similar for Canadians, Aussies, Kiwis, and other “developed” nations.).

If you want to move to France, you have four main options:.

Industry observers note that the student visa is pretty straightforward. You need to enroll in a full-time university program and show you have enough funds to support yourself (around 600 Euros per month). A friend is presently there on this visa, as she is doing a nine-month intensive French program to become fluent. You still have to apply for the visa, but if you’re enrolled in an accredited school, you’ll likely get approved. Another benefit to this visa is that you can work part-time on it!

Recent findings suggest that but this visa is contingent on being in school, so if you leave or quit, it’s voided. However, when you are done, you can change this to a “job seeker” visa, which can give you up to another six months in France (or more depending on how long your program was).

I thought about applying for the entrepreneur visa, but the application process is pretty complex and can take months to be approved. You have to set up your business in France — and that is a lot of paperwork. You have to show that your business makes money, has clients (at least one of them being French), and can support you full-time (you have to make at least the French minimum wage). They will scrutinize your assets and financials a lot and you’ll need to register your business in France and pay French taxes.

Sources indicate that additionally, France offers a talent visa. If you’re an expert in your field (with verifiable accreditations and accolades), this could be a good visa to apply for, especially if you proposal to stay in France for a long time and want to physically work there. But, again, you’ll need to have some source of income and plan to do physical business in France. If you’re not an academic but someone in the arts, you have to show how you are going to add to the “culture of France” in some way.

While I would meet the requirements for both those visas, the process for either would have been time-consuming, and, since I’m not sure France is going to be my forever home, I decided not to go through that process.

Industry observers note that so I went with the long-term visitor visa, officially called VLS-TS visiteur. This allows me to stay up to 12 months in France and is renewable in the country. It does come with a lot of restrictions, however: I can’t physically work here and I am not allowed into the French social welfare system.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also the visa a lot of Americans (and most retirees) are coming in on. If you have passive income or retirement savings and just want to live in France, this is a good option for you. It allows you to set up a bank account and it can be renewed pretty much indefinitely.

The paperwork for this visa (which I’ll get into in a bit) essentially comes down to whether or not you can support yourself. French authorities want to make sure you won’t be a burden on the system.

According to recent reports, my biggest question centered around whether or not I could “work” on this visa. A lot of creators and digital nomads are applying for — and getting — this visa.

But remember: you aren’t allowed to work on this visa so how are you going to work if you can’t work?

So let me take a moment to talk about “work” from a legal standpoint.

As I mentioned, there’s no digital nomad visa that allows you to work in France. And the French tax office said last July that remote work is considered taxable — but there are no official laws that say so. That’s just their opinion and there’s been no progress in codifying that opinion. In fact, my visa doesn’t even come with a tax number, so I can’t be taxed. I couldn’t pay taxes even if I wanted to.

The visa office asks how you’ll support yourself when you are in France and one of the sources of income they accept is “income from work.” I was very open that my means of support would be the income from this blog and my books.

Sources indicate that the system there really hasn’t caught up to remote work. It still defines “work” as something you do physically that could take away a job from a French person.

It has been revealed that so could I run walking tours in Paris? Nope. Could you work at a café? Nope.

But does writing this blog post count as work? After all, no one is paying for it. It’s a free resource. Does going to a café to work on the next great American novel count? What about my weekly newsletter that has affiliate links (that generate income) in it? Is writing that considered work?

Sources indicate that the gray area is considerable, so the best thing to do is to talk to a lawyer. I recommend Daniel Tostado (yes, that’s his real name), one of the biggest American-French immigration lawyers in Paris. He has a huge law firm and regularly meets with government officials to clarify the rules on this. He gave me some solid advice.

In a recent development, for this long-term visitor visa, the application process is pretty easy. You go to the French government website, fill out your application, take the application number to the TLScontact website, and make an appointment. (France outsources the appointment process to this organization, which then sends everything to the French consulate for approval.).

According to recent reports, the main things you’ll want to demonstrate are that you have accommodation for 90 days on your application and enough income to support yourself. They just want to make sure you aren’t going to be a burden on the system. I went overboard. Here’s what I brought to my appointment:.

It has been revealed that I didn’t need the second bank account, tax returns, or W-2 (they weren’t required) but the woman at the appointment remarked the more proof you had the better and it wouldn’t hurt. And another friend who got this visa didn’t bring anything beyond what was asked in the application form. But I wanted to take no chances!

At the appointment, the staff double-checks your paperwork, takes your biometric data, collects the fees, and then sends your passport to the embassy for processing. Officially, it takes up to 15 days to process your visa, but everyone I know seems to get it back within a week.

Industry observers note that the worst part was not knowing if you are approved until your passport is returned. While you can track the progress of your application, you don’t know the verdict until your passport is back in your hands. While I was waiting (and anxiously spiraling), I looked on Reddit and found that most denials were for lack of income or challenges with their accommodation, which seem to be the two most key things to have perfect on your application.

Once you get your visa back, you can enter France any time after the start date. After you enter, you have 90 days to register your visa with the state (they give you a little QR code with instructions). This allows you to “officially” be on this long-term visa. (It’s a more paperwork kind of thing.).

Once that is done, there’s nothing else to do and you can stay in France (and Europe) until your visa expires!

It has been revealed that so, if you’re considering moving to France, these are your options. But, as always, I’m not a lawyer and this is not legal advice. In regard to work and other complications or questions, it’s vital that you seek legal counsel and get their expert opinion!

Breaking: Rep. Ken Calvert wins all-Republican race in California

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ken Calvert walks down the House steps after votes on Sept.
  • Young Kim in a redrawn Southern California district that pitted the two Republicans against one another.
  • Calvert was leading his rival by 7 points Monday night when The Associated Press called the race for California’s 40th District with more than 70 percent of the vote in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

California Rep. Ken Calvert walks down the House steps after votes on Sept. 3. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

Rep. Ken Calvert defeated Rep. Young Kim in a redrawn Southern California district that pitted the two Republicans against one another.

Calvert was leading his rival by 7 points Monday night when The Associated Press called the race for California’s 40th District with more than 70 percent of the vote in.

Calvert, who chairs the powerful House Defense Appropriations Subcommittee, is the longest-serving Republican in the California delegation, first winning election to Congress in 1992.

It has been revealed that the race was reshaped by the Golden State’s newly introduced voter-approved House map, drawn by state Democrats in response to mid-decade redistricting by Texas Republicans. The new map dismantled Calvert’s 41st District in Riverside County, transforming it into a safely blue Democratic seat in the Los Angeles area. That prompted him to run for the redrawn 40th District, which included a sizable percentage of his current constituents.

Industry observers note that the rare intraparty general election was possible because Calvert and Kim finished in the top two slots in the state’s June primary. Under the California system, all candidates run on the same primary ballot, with the top two vote-getters, regardless of party, advancing to November.

Calvert had already declared victory last week, saying on social media that there was “no greater honor than serving my neighbors and our communities in Congress.”.

Kim’s defeat is the second of her congressional career — she lost her initial bid during the 2018 blue wave before winning election to the House two years later.

In her concession message, Kim singled out California Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom, who led the redistricting effort last year that targeted five Republican-held districts. Democrats flipped all five seats last week.

“It’s unfortunate that Gavin Newsom’s political redistricting scheme forced two Republican members from Congress into this race,’’ she noted in a statement.

According to recent reports, the race between was marked by rancor, with Calvert alleging that Kim was not a true conservative and supported higher taxes. Kim accused Calvert of growing rich off stock trades over his decades in Washington.

Calvert will serve in a delegation with a dramatically smaller GOP presence next year, with Democrats likely to hold 48 of California’s 52 House seats. Just two other California Republicans – Reps. Vince Fong and Tom McClintock – have been reelected so far, while a third, Rep. Jay Obernolte, narrowly leads his Democratic challenger in an as-yet-uncalled race.

The Calvert-Kim battle was not the only all-party November clash in California, with several districts featuring matchups between two Democrats.

Industry observers note that one incumbent has already been unseated, with Rep. Jimmy Gomez losing to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres in the Los Angeles-area 34th District, according to The Associated Press.

Two other blue-on-blue contests in Northern California remained uncalled as of Tuesday afternoon: Rep. Mike Thompson was trailing venture capitalist Eric Jones in the 4th District, while Rep. Doris Matsui led Sacramento City Councilmember Mai Vang in the 7th District.

Industry News: Inside NYC’s Pool Scene, the City’s Great Equalizer

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Just when we thought Newly introduced York had seen it all, I caught wind that the first-ever five-borough pool tournament—in the city’s history—was about to kick off.
  • It has been revealed that it was all thanks to Dan Tran, the brains behind the Five Boro Break.
  • Dan Tran, the brains behind the Five Boro Break, has been shooting pool across the city for more than a decade.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when we thought Newly introduced York had seen it all, I caught wind that the first-ever five-borough pool tournament—in the city’s history—was about to kick off.

It has been revealed that it was all thanks to Dan Tran, the brains behind the Five Boro Break. Tran has been shooting pool across the city for more than a decade and has played on more than 130 tables out of the 400 to 500 he estimates are in NYC (he even catalogs them out of his own goodwill for other Upcoming Yorkers, on Pool Tables NYC). He’s just that guy: an absolute force of nature with a heavy case of do-the-impossible syndrome. One day over summer, at a league night with fellow pool-playing regulars, he wondered if there was a way to get folks like these together for one big game—to unite New York’s pool-playing dive bar families and play as one.

Dan Tran, the brains behind the Five Boro Break, has been shooting pool across the city for more than a decade.

Recent findings suggest that the idea was a tournament “built by pool players, run by pool players,” says Tran, who you’ll most often find playing at George & Jacks in Williamsburg. “No money changing hands, no ulterior motive.” Just bringing together this community, which Tran is the first to admit existed long before he stepped on the scene.

Sources indicate that so this powerhouse did it: 256 players, 16 venues, all five boroughs, over two days in early November. When I caught up with Tran the week before the tournament, he still couldn’t believe he was bringing the idea to life. “I was like, 'What am I signing up to do once I post this?' But then I posted it, and it just took off—like completely took off. And everybody was like, 'Yeah, we can totally do this.'”.

I rode the wave of Tran’s infectious energy and spent an entire weekend hopping between dives watching the tournament’s pool players do what they do best.

The audience at NYC bar Sugar Mouse applauds Five Boro Break creator Dan Tran at the finals.

Sources indicate that on Saturday, November 7, you could feel it in the air. There was something electric about knowing the grittiest corners of Fresh York City were locked in on the same game. That distinct four o’clock autumn sunlight was shining on Bushwick Ice House, one of the 16 venues, when I walked in with Traveler’s Julia Abbonizio and Skyli Alvarez, who were ready to photograph the scene. Gathered around a red-felt table were a dozen or so players who shot us “what’s up” nods as we entered; the bartender moseyed over with “what’s it gonna be?” eyes. Without a word exchanged, we were already part of the bar’s family.

In a recent development, the crowd around us was dressed in their dive-bar best (jeans), and glowing under the neon-red Budweiser lights. The energy in the room matched the game unfolding. One moment, the place roared with Miller High Life clinks and friends catching up. The next it would go pin-drop silent as someone bent over and lined up a shot. More often than not, we’d hear a “nice” before the cue even struck, or a congratulatory clap before someone sank the 8-ball, because everyone knew the game well enough to see exactly what was coming.

Will Pay, a Bushwick Ice House regular, designed the tournament's felt-green shirts.

Satoe Onizuka plays Netta Rawner (left) at Bushwick Ice House.

Will Pay, a Bushwick resident and the creative mind behind the tournament’s T-shirt and site design—dark green, like a pool table’s felt, and featuring a solid orange 5-ball to nod to the boroughs—was running the show. He jokingly told me he’s something of a pool scout around the city, sniffing out the best shooters to join his league. Pay attested that, when Tran initially announced the tournament, interest at his local dive Bushwick Ice House was immediate. Within 10 minutes of the link being live, the waitlist to play at the venue had passed 100.

Recent findings suggest that while Satoe Onizuka, the stealthiest star of the regulars, shook another hand after winning yet another round, I snuck outside of Bushwick Ice House to chat with Pay, who was wearing the Five Boro Break shirt he designed. We got into the type of conversation you do at a dive bar or around a pool table. The love of the game. The importance of dives as sacred spaces. The alluring seediness of it all. Pay knows how we got here: “The game itself is called billiards, but it got casualized to ‘pool’ because people used to throw a ton of money on the table—pool their money—and gamble,” Pay said. “Obviously, that’s gone out the window because everyone’s super chill these days, but what’s cool is that it still has that air of danger, of being something a bit forbidden.” Will’s right: it’s never corny to shoot pool. No matter who you are, it makes you feel like the slickest person in the room.

There’s also that sense that you’re part of something bigger. Back inside, Pay gestured around the room. “Look at this place,” he said in admiration. “There’s literally no real estate for this table. But it’s here. And without it, this place would simply not be what it is. These people would probably not be here in this bar. I don’t even think this bar would exist.”.

According to recent reports, the enthusiasm at Bushwick Ice House reminded me of how this tournament could only have happened because NYC dive bars already operate as tight-knit communities of their own. They’re the ultimate third places, the spots that aren’t home or work—and the pool table is, in fact, their beating heart.

By 9 p.m. on Saturday, when we stumbled into LES’ Sadie’s Ward, '80s dance-pop shook the walls. Drinks were flowing, the room glowed disco-lit, and everyone was having such a good time you had to shout to be heard by the person next to you. A group of hodge-podge regulars stood two and three deep around the pool table, watching the small, curly-haired Amanda Andries, one of the bar’s most beloved shooters, sink her way toward Sunday’s finals.

Industry observers note that andries is one of the Ladies of Sadie’s, a magnetic group of female regulars at this bar, who were gassing each other up and out-shooting all the 6-foot-something men in flannels that dared to play them. For all the history that tables at bars like Sadie’s have absorbed, it’s the people gathered around them who make the pool scene so captivating—and at this bar, the social fabric is very tightly knit.

East Williamsburg's Anchored Inn was one of the 16 bars that hosted Five Boro Break games.

We sat in the small hideaway across from the bar as the games rolled on, reflecting on the players we’d met throughout the tournament so far: soft-spoken, sharp-shooting Audrey Jones at Anchored Inn over loaded Carmen fries; Allegra “Legz” Fierro outside the graffied, mirrorless bathroom at Blue Ruin Bar; and Elvin Estevez, a polite killer on the table, in the leather booths at Twins Lounge. I’d asked each to tell me their golden rule of playing pool in this city, but it all came back to one recurring theme: be a good person. There’s a camaraderie in wanting to keep NYC’s pool scene a sacred place.

It’s easy not to suck, though. Sam Shumway of Pool Table Archive said to me by phone in the days following the event. Five years ago, he started posting photos of the pool tables he’d played on in cities across the US, but his hobby grew into a living record of pool culture.

In a recent development, “Pool tables are special because they’re a snapshot of a time and a place in a bar,” he told me. “A lot of these tables are older than you are. Like, that’s a 40-year-old table. Imagine how much life it’s seen around it.” You can picture a montage of scenes immediately: 4 a.m. closings, birthday toasts, new friendships, awkward first dates, breakups, and more than a few questionable decisions. Maybe a win in the first-ever cross-city tournament.

Allegra “Legz” Fierro in Hell's Kitchen's Blue Ruin Bar, just before a match.

Come Sunday, we walked into a jam-packed, purple-lit Sugar Mouse for the finals. The winners from each of the 16 bars would go head-to-head across two pool tables. A live dad rock band jammed in the corner, and all I saw were familiar faces from Saturday’s hijinks, smiling, watching respectfully, nodding when a friend nailed a shot, and hugging and shaking hands when one missed. As the field dwindled to four semifinalists, then just two, the crowd drew tighter around the remaining table. Two large projectors cast a live feed onto the wall, as former WPBA No. 1 Jennifer Barretta commented and Hall of Famer John Leyman refereed with a stern eye.

We were all there for the moment Brennan Brooks of the BCA Brooklyn Travel League took the inaugural win, cementing his right to take home that iconic sign. But as I took in the room around me, what stood out most was seeing people packed in like sardines to watch their fellow dive bar regulars take the stage. It was a kaleidoscope of communities, each representing their local with love. The Five Boro Break was never just about winning; it was about creating a space where everyone could be part of something.

A triumphant moment at Sadie's Ward on the Lower East Side.

The East Village's Sugar Mouse hosted the tournament final.

Sources indicate that it was a fresh alternative to life on a screen—maybe that’s part of why so many people highlighted up. “People are craving human connection again; people are craving something to do with their hands,” Shumway had noted. And though it might look too cool, or intimidating, everyone has a place if they want it. “Pool brings together people who would normally have nothing in common. And there are no pre-qualifications for putting your name on a chalkboard. You might get beat, and that’s okay.”.

Recent findings suggest that at the end of the Finals night, all of us riding a collective high, Tran stood next to the championship table to thank everyone who helped bring his vision to life. He couldn’t get a word out before the room burst into applause. Thirty seconds of it, and it revealed no signs of letting up. Humble as he is, he just smiled.

Tran rattled off the bars, businesses, and people who stepped up to make the tournament possible, shaking his head happily. “This is what pool does,” he said. “It brings people together rather than pushes people apart.”.

Or as Shumway likes to put it: “Pool is the great equalizer.”.

#77160. Industry News: Don’t Visit Ko Lipe

📅 23 Feb 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1246 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nomadicmatt ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Don’t Visit Ko Lipe

📅 23 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, after 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006.
  • There was much to do here but that was the point.
  • Sources indicate that it was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006. Back then, it was one of those super off-the-beaten-path destinations that few but the most intrepid travelers visited, where electricity only ran a few hours a day, basic bungalows right on the beach cost something like $2 USD, and there really was a last boat for the season.

There was much to do here but that was the point. You hung out on the beach, read a book, went snorkeling, went back to the beach, drank beers at the one beach bar on the island, rotated meals between the five restaurants there, and went to bed early.

Sources indicate that it was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck. Days easily turned into weeks here.

If you asked me what the highlight of all my travels was, I would be the time I spent on Ko Lipe. I made incredible friends, lounged around, got to know the locals, learned a bit of Thai, and, overall, lived that idyllic backpacker life we all dream about.

Over the years, I’ve avoided going back to Ko Lipe because the memory of my time there is so strong that I didn’t want to ruin it. Any re-visit would simply be trying to recreated a magic that couldn’t be recreated because the people that it special wouldn’t be there. I’d be chasing travel ghosts. And, since I know my sleepy paradise has been developed greatly over the years, I was also too afraid seeing that would make me sad.

Recent findings suggest that tourism in Thailand tends toward the unsustainable. No island really develops in a good way. It’s all build, build, build.

And I didn’t want to see my Ko Lipe like that.

But as I was planning my recent trip through Southeast Asia, returning to Ko Lipe made sense. I was heading down the Indian Ocean side of Thailand on my way into Malaysia and I’d pass by it.

It has been revealed that and, since I was looking for a lively place for New Year’s Eve, it seemed liked the best choice. I knew there would be travelers there and there were no other nearby islands that would work, especially since Ko Lipe has a boat to Langkawi, which was my next stop.

And I’m sad to report that Ko Lipe took the Ko Phi Phi model of tourism and is now extremely overdeveloped.

Industry observers note that most of the island is now paved over, the old dirt footpaths having become concrete for the cars and construction trucks. Swaths of palm trees are now the sites of high-end resorts with pools (on an island with no natural water supply). Construction of more resorts continues at a fast pace. The coral around the island is dying, a victim of all the boats, anchors, pollution, and overfishing. Beaches are now lined with boats, their exhaust spilling into the ocean, leaving a shiny film you can see as you swim. And the restaurants cater to tourists looking for bad Western food, not great Thai cuisine.

The island’s boom has displaced many locals, who were forced to sell to mainland developers, and much of the island’s workforce is now from the mainland. They see little of the benefits this tourism boom.

So lies Ko Lipe, another victim of Thailand’s all too common overdevelopment and exploitation of limited resources.

According to recent reports, I met lots of people there who loved the island. If it’s your first time, I can see why you would love it. After all, the area is postcard perfect, the water is perfectly an azure blue, the sand is a beautiful white, and since you’re surrounded by a national park, a lot of tours take you to some secluded islands.

And, in comparison to Ko Phi Phi, Krabi, or Phuket, it is less developed so I can’t fault someone stepping here for the first time going “wow!”.

But, as I reflect on the island and its overdevelopment, I have come to the same conclusion I have about Ko Phi Phi: people shouldn’t visit.

I’m not against growth, but I’m against this kind of growth. It’s not sustainably managed and going there will only tax the island’s limited resources even further. You can’t put the genie back in the bottle and no local is going to say “sure, I’ll stay broke so you can an idealized vision of the world.”.

And, with so many other islands to visit that are well managed (Ko Lanta, Ko Jum, and Ko Mook, to name three nearby), I think you should skip Ko Lipe.

A visit there will only make things worse.

It pains me to say that, because it was such a beautiful place, and my original visit had a huge impact on my life. But if we’re going to be good stewards and travelers, sometimes you just have to say enough is enough.

And Ko Lipe is a place where enough is enough.

Go somewhere else that is better managed.

Because your choices do have an impact.

Riding elephants in Thailand went away when consumers became more conscious of it. Eco lodges got big because of consumers. Overtourism is talked about by consumers as much as it is by locals.

Maybe if enough people start to do something, Ko Lipe will change.

But, at the very least, by not going you are at least no contributing to the problem.

Industry News: Can You Pack Power Banks in Checked Luggage? 2026 Airline Battery Rules Travellers Need to Know

📅 09 Jul 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most travellers now fly with several battery-powered items: a phone, laptop, tablet, camera, headphones, smartwatch, portable charger or vape.
  • Industry observers note that in 2026, aviation safety authorities are warning travellers to pay closer attention to lithium batteries after reports that millions of batteries are still being packed incorrectly.
  • It has been revealed that they belong in your carry-on bag or personal item, where they can be reached quickly if they overheat, smoke or catch fire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most travellers now fly with several battery-powered items: a phone, laptop, tablet, camera, headphones, smartwatch, portable charger or vape. But packing one of them in the wrong bag can cause real problems at the airport.

Industry observers note that in 2026, aviation safety authorities are warning travellers to pay closer attention to lithium batteries after reports that millions of batteries are still being packed incorrectly. The biggest mistake is simple: power banks, portable chargers and spare lithium batteries should not go in checked luggage.

It has been revealed that they belong in your carry-on bag or personal item, where they can be reached quickly if they overheat, smoke or catch fire. This matters even more when your carry-on gets taken away at the gate and sent underneath the plane.

Sources indicate that no. Power banks, portable chargers and spare lithium batteries should not be packed in checked luggage. They belong in your carry-on bag or personal item, where they can be reached promptly if they overheat.The same goes for loose camera batteries, spare laptop batteries, rechargeable battery packs, vape devices and phone battery charging cases. If your carry-on bag is taken away at the gate and checked underneath the plane, remove all power banks and spare batteries before handing it over.Phones, laptops, tablets and cameras with batteries installed are treated differently from spare batteries, but the safest habit is still to keep valuable battery-powered electronics in the cabin whenever possible. If an airline allows a device to be checked, it should be completely powered off, protected from damage and prevented from turning on accidentally.

The safest habit is simple: power banks, spare batteries and removable batteries stay with you. Valuable electronics are usually better in the cabin too.

Power banks are not allowed in checked luggage because they contain lithium batteries that can overheat if damaged, poorly packed, overcharged, exposed to heat or affected by a defect.

According to recent reports, in rare cases, lithium batteries can enter thermal runaway. That means the battery heats faster than it can cool itself down. It may swell, smoke, burn or ignite.

Industry observers note that if that happens in the cabin, passengers and crew can spot the problem promptly. Cabin crews are trained to respond to battery incidents. If the battery is hidden inside a suitcase in the cargo hold, it is much harder to access.

That is why this rule is not just airport red tape. A small charger in the wrong bag can become a serious safety issue.

Before you check a suitcase, look for anything with a loose, spare or removable lithium battery.

These items should stay in your carry-on or personal item:.

You should also think carefully before checking valuable electronics with installed batteries, including:.

Some airlines may allow certain devices with batteries installed in checked luggage if they are completely powered off and protected from damage. But for most travellers, the smarter choice is to keep electronics in the cabin.

Recent findings suggest that checked bags get dropped, delayed, searched and occasionally sent on their own little vacation. Your laptop does not need that character-building experience.

This is where the rules confuse a lot of travellers.

A spare battery is any battery that is not installed inside the device it powers. A power bank also counts because it is an external battery used to charge other devices.

Recent findings suggest that A battery installed in a device is different. This includes the battery built into your phone, laptop, tablet, camera, headphones or smartwatch.

The easiest rule to remember is this:.

If the battery is loose, removable or used to charge something else, do not check it. The FAA’s lithium battery guidance says power banks and spare lithium batteries must travel in carry-on baggage, not checked luggage.

Gate-checking is one of the easiest ways to accidentally break the battery rule.

You may pack your power bank correctly in your carry-on at home. Then you reach the gate, the overhead bins are full and the agent tags your carry-on to go underneath the plane.

At that moment, your carry-on has become checked luggage.

Before handing it over, remove:.

Sources indicate that the easiest system is to keep all power banks and spare batteries in one small pouch inside your personal item. If your roller bag gets gate-checked, you can remove the pouch in seconds instead of digging through your suitcase while the boarding line gives you the collective death stare.

Airlines measure lithium-ion battery size in watt-hours, written as Wh.

Most standard phone power banks are under 100 Wh and are usually allowed in carry-on baggage. Larger batteries may require airline approval, and very large batteries are generally not allowed in normal passenger baggage.

The 100 Wh rule matters most for large laptop power banks, professional camera gear, video equipment and drone batteries.

Industry observers note that A typical 10,000 mAh power bank is often around 37 Wh. A 20,000 mAh power bank is often around 74 Wh. Larger power banks can get close to the limit, so check before you pack.

According to CATSA’s battery packing guidelines, travellers should keep batteries and electronic devices containing batteries in their carry-on baggage, avoid damaged or recalled batteries, and protect spare batteries from short-circuiting.

Recent findings suggest that look for the Wh rating printed on the back, bottom or side of the power bank. Newer batteries often show this number clearly.

If the label only highlights mAh and volts, you can calculate watt-hours with this formula:.

Since 1,000 mAh equals 1 Ah, a 20,000 mAh power bank is 20 Ah.

That would usually fall under the 100 Wh carry-on limit.

In a recent development, if the label has rubbed off and the airline cannot confirm the battery rating, the item may be refused. Do not rely on guessing at the airport.

Laptops, phones and tablets have batteries installed inside the device, so they are not treated the same way as loose spare batteries or power banks.

However, airline rules vary. If an airline allows these devices in checked luggage, they should be completely powered off, protected from damage and packed so they cannot accidentally turn on.

That means fully powered off, not sleeping, hibernating or sitting there quietly planning to wake up mid-flight.

In a recent development, in practice, keep phones, laptops and tablets in the cabin whenever possible. They are valuable, easy to damage and often essential if your checked bag is delayed.

In a recent development, no. Vapes and e-cigarettes should not be packed in checked luggage because they contain batteries. They should travel in the cabin and must not be used or charged during the flight.

In a recent development, rules for vaping products also vary by destination, and some countries restrict or ban them. If an adult is legally travelling with one, it still needs to follow airline battery rules.

Recent findings suggest that if you are packing for someone else, check for these before closing a checked suitcase. A vape tossed into checked luggage can create the same battery concern as other lithium-powered devices.

Smart luggage can usually be checked only if the battery can be removed.

In a recent development, A smart bag is luggage with built-in charging, tracking or other battery-powered features. If the bag is going into the cabin and meets carry-on size limits, it may be accepted as a carry-on. If it has to be checked, the battery must usually be removed and brought into the cabin.

If the battery cannot be removed, the airline may refuse to accept the bag as checked luggage.

According to recent reports, before travelling with smart luggage, find the battery compartment at home. Do not wait until the check-in counter to discover that the “removable” battery requires a tiny screwdriver, a prayer and the patience of a saint.

The drone or camera body may be allowed in checked luggage by some airlines, but spare lithium batteries should be removed and carried in the cabin.

Spare camera batteries and drone batteries should be individually protected so the terminals cannot touch metal or each other. Use the original packaging, a battery case, a protective pouch or tape over exposed terminals.

Recent findings suggest that if you travel with several batteries for photography or video work, check your airline’s quantity limits before you fly. Battery rules can be stricter for professional video gear and larger drone batteries.

It has been revealed that loose batteries should never be thrown into a bag with coins, keys, jewellery, cables or other metal objects. Battery terminals can short-circuit if they touch metal.

This is especially important for camera batteries, drone batteries and loose rechargeable cells.

Do not travel with a battery that is swollen, cracked, leaking, unusually hot, damaged or recalled.

A swollen power bank is not “probably fine.” It is a damaged battery and should be taken to an appropriate recycling or disposal location.

In a recent development, before flying with an older power bank, check the model number and look for current recall notices from the manufacturer or your government recall site. Some recalled power banks may be prohibited onboard entirely.

Industry observers note that if a battery looks questionable, leave it at home. Replacing a charger is cheaper than dealing with a safety incident at the airport.

If a battery or device becomes hot, starts swelling, smokes, sparks or smells strange during a flight, tell the cabin crew immediately.

Do not put it in the overhead bin. Do not hide it in a bag. Do not take it to the washroom. Cabin crew are trained to respond to battery incidents, but they need to know right away.

Recent findings suggest that the goal is not to handle the problem yourself. The goal is to alert the people trained to deal with it.

Before leaving for the airport, do this quick check:.

This takes less than two minutes and can prevent a pulled bag, confiscated item or airport delay.

Before you check a suitcase or hand over a carry-on at the gate, make sure:.

Before you check any bag, open it and look for batteries.

Recent findings suggest that power banks, portable chargers, spare batteries and removable lithium batteries stay with you in the cabin. Phones, laptops, tablets and cameras are usually safer in your carry-on. If your carry-on gets taken at the gate, remove your battery pouch before the bag goes underneath the plane.

Industry observers note that the goal is not to stop travelling with electronics. The goal is to stop packing them on autopilot.

A two-minute battery check before every flight can save your bag, your gear and possibly your travel day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Odyssey of the Seas has returned to its homeport in the Latest York region for a winter season offering cruises to the Bahamas and the Caribbean.

Having completed a seasonal deployment in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Greek Islands, the Royal Caribbean vessel arrived in Cape Liberty on November 8, 2026.

Before kicking off its winter season, the 2021-built vessel operated a trans-Atlantic crossing that started in Civitavecchia, Italy.

The 14-night repositioning voyage included visits to destinations in Spain and Portugal.

Odyssey’s New York season starts with a series of seven-night cruises to the Bahamas and Florida, which sail to Nassau and Port Canaveral.

The itineraries are also highlighted by visits to Royal Caribbean’s private island destination of Perfect Day at CocoCay.

Starting in January, the vessel will also offer longer cruises to the Eastern Caribbean, operating 11- and 12-night cruises to ports of call that include Bridgetown in Barbados, Charlotte Amalie in St. Thomas and St. John’s in Antigua.

The season runs through late April, when the Odyssey of the Seas is scheduled to embark on a repositioning voyage back to Europe.

Sailing from Cape Liberty to Civitavecchia, the 14-night cruise will feature visits to destinations in Portugal, Spain and Italy, including Ponta Delgada, Málaga, Cartagena and La Spezia.

The ship is scheduled to embark on another summer season in the Mediterranean in early November, offering weeklong cruises to the Greek Islands and Italy.

Completing five years of service in 2026, the Odyssey of the Seas underwent a routine drydock before its summer season.

The 4,200-passenger vessel underwent technical maintenance during the shipyard stay, in addition to overall upkeep work on public areas and staterooms.

Built at the Meyer Werft shipyard in Papenburg, Germany, the ship is part of Royal Caribbean’s Quantum-class series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is Write Here, a column where authors and literary luminaries tell us about the travels they took to find inspiration and create their latest books.

In this installment, author and n+1 editor Chad Harbach describes his love for Block Island, Rhode Island, and a 2016 trip that informed a keystone part of his latest novel The Brightness. In the book, a bildungsroman that tackles topics like campus politics, the discourse around sexual assault, and the anxiety of being in one’s twenties, Block Island serves as the dramatic setting for a long, eventful wedding night that alters the lives of Harbach’s characters—particularly that of Pella Affenlicht, who originally appeared in Harbach’s 2011 debut The Art of Fielding. Below, Harbach recalls gathering his own friends for a summer holiday on Block Island as an excuse to refamiliarize himself with the destination as he began to write it in fiction—and the local peafowl that nearly made it into the book.

According to recent reports, “In the early stages of writing The Brightness, one of the first things I decided was that the book’s centerpiece, the big wedding of the character Owen, would be located on Block Island, Rhode Island. I wanted the scene—which is now this 150-page stretch of the story, when all sorts of crazy things happen over a single, almost Shakespearean night—to be on the island’s eastern shore where houses are positioned at the top of these stone cliffs. I pictured an outdoor dance floor overlooking the beach and the ocean with the moon in the distance. Essentially I wanted to write the destination wedding I desperately wanted to attend. But as I was working on it, I realized I needed to go back there to check if my memories of the place were accurate, to have it fresh in my mind.

My then-partner and I organized a trip to Block Island with a large group of friends in the summer of 2016. We rented a massive house and folks came from places like Fresh York, Philadelphia, California, and Amsterdam. It felt like a wedding in that sense—everyone gathered for this joyous celebration in a beautiful place. We didn’t do all the terrible stuff to one another that’s maybe required for the juicy plot of a novel, but we did spend eight days cooking together, playing the piano, singing songs, drinking a lot, and staying up very late.

Sources indicate that but we couldn’t sleep in very late because, well, there were these peahens. There was a sort of farm with animals, maybe a petting zoo, near our house, and their peahens liked to come and roost in the trees on our property. Every morning at 5 a.m., after we had been up until 2 or 3 a.m., the peahens would just start. I don’t know if you’ve ever heard the squawking of peahens, but suffice to say it was awful. It’s funny: When I started doing publicity for The Brightness, an announcement mentioned that part of it is set on Block Island. I got texts from friends who were on that trip, saying, congrats, we’re so excited, the fucking peahens better be in there. I initially did have this whole bit about the peahens, but there was so much going on in the plot that I cut them—not without really trying to make it work first.

Other than the loud birds, it was a great trip. The place struck me as just as magical as it had when I first went at 19 years old, when I was in college. I had a friend whose grandparents had a house there. I’ve visited several times since, and always loved it. But this was the only time I’ve ever gone somewhere for book research, and I was able to lock in some granular details like what the downtown looks like, the shape of the buildings, the sight of the marshlands, and what it’s like to bike out to the airport.

I was also excited to find that the feel of it was exactly as I remembered. Block Island has this rugged, natural beauty—it’s a rocky, tree-filled place surrounded by ocean, where everyone just rides bikes around, and part of it is a protected nature preserve. It’s sort of the forgotten sibling of Nantucket or Martha’s Vineyard. Some people don’t even know that Block Island exists, which keeps it from changing too much, even though it was settled by Europeans in the mid-1600s. The cemetery there has the tombstones of families that date back centuries, long before the United States became a country. I think some of those same families still live on the island now. So there’s this sense of continuity and timelessness.

Even before you reach Block Island, there’s just something about climbing on to the ferry and heading out into the open water, this freedom and openness that’s very inspiring to me. I grew up in Wisconsin, on Lake Michigan, which isn’t an ocean but looks like one, and I’ve always loved that feeling of vastness and mystery that comes with a massive body of water—that literal depth. It reminds me that we as humans actually haven’t mastered everything, and there are many things in this world that are not easy for us to touch.

All of this made Block Island a helpful setting in The Brightness. What happens on this wedding night propels the characters toward life paths that are very different from what they thought they were going to have, and having the story be imbued with the island’s sense of openness, possibility, and what might be feels fitting. As a writer, that can be part of the work: tapping into that feeling or gestalt of a place. It can be very easy to do at times, and difficult at others. And, you know, sometimes it’s just hard to write. So it was a great help writing about somewhere I love visiting literally and creatively. Instead of resisting sitting down at my desk, I’d be like, I’m ready to go to Block Island. It’s this setting I could picture well, enjoy being in, and keep traveling to—even if it was just in my imagination.” —As told to Matt Ortile.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, center, arrives for a House Republican leadership candidate forum for the 120th Congress in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday, with Rep. Celeste Maloy, R-Utah, walking alongside him. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

House Republicans on Tuesday opted for a latest face atop their ranks, electing Rep. Jim Jordan as the incoming minority leader for the 120th Congress after Republicans suffered massive losses in last week’s midterm elections.

The Ohio Republican defeated outgoing Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., in a closed-door, secret-ballot election. The final tally was 106-73.

Industry observers note that “Over the next two years, House Republicans will fight for American families. Democrats offer more government. We will offer more freedom,” Jordan stated after the hourslong process.

The two had been working the phones before making their pitches during a candidates forum in the Capitol Visitor Center’s auditorium on Tuesday morning. Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., unveiled last week he would not seek a leadership post in the newly introduced Congress, which will be seated on Jan. 3.

“Obviously Jim and I know each other, but I’ve got a proven record of how to bring people together,” Scalise said ahead of the vote, trying to play up his experience, including more than a decade on the leadership team that included a stint as whip.

As House Republicans trickled out of the candidates’ forum for breaks or to take phone calls, one member, granted anonymity to discuss a private session, remarked Scalise and Jordan “both have strong points, but they both have flaws.” Each made an unsuccessful bid for speaker in 2023 after the ouster of Kevin McCarthy, before the gavel ultimately went to Johnson.

Declining to reveal which would get his vote, the member noted: “I won’t talk about a secret vote, but I know who I think is best to lead us.”.

The incoming minority conference also selected other leaders on Tuesday.

It has been revealed that majority Whip Tom Emmer of Minnesota held off a challenge from Texas Rep. August Pfluger to become minority whip in January, despite some grumbling about how tight votes were handled on the floor this year.

According to recent reports, “We’ve got to retool our whip operation,” Texas Rep. Nathaniel Moran noted Tuesday morning, pointing to “the number of times we were held up by either discharge petitions or failed rule votes.”.

“Those were things that should not have happened in the majority,” said Moran as he publicly backed Pfluger for whip.

But Emmer projected confidence after his whip win, comparing the moment to when Republicans were down and out after their losses in 2018 only to rebound a few years later.

Recent findings suggest that “To our colleagues on the left, enjoy this honeymoon phase, because come Jan. 3, 2027, you will regret ever putting your name on a ballot,” he said at a news conference, adding that Republicans under his watch would expose the “empty promises” that Democrats made to voters and push back on what he called their “radical” agenda.

In a recent development, in the day’s only three-way race, conference Chair Lisa McClain of Michigan defeated Reps. Erin Houchin of Indiana and Greg Steube of Florida to keep her spot.

It has been revealed that “We had a spirited leadership election. There were important conversations about the future of our conference, and I listened,” McClain stated at the news conference.

In the race to lead House Republicans’ campaign arm, Rep. Brian Jack of Georgia defeated Rep. Rudy Yakym of Indiana, seen as an up-and-coming Ways and Means Committee member. That means Jack will take on a huge share of the uphill task of selecting candidates and raising funds for the 2028 cycle as he helms the National Republican Congressional Committee.

But most of the attention heading into Tuesday’s closed-door proceedings was on the minority leader race.

Johnson, the outgoing speaker, declined to endorse a candidate but had encouraging words for Jordan after his win. “He’s going to do an excellent job. He’s a good, trusted friend and brother,” he said.

Rep. Tom Cole, R-Okla., stated it was a “tough choice for the conference to make,” but he wasn’t disappointed in the pick. “He was an exceptionally capable chairman of both Oversight and Judiciary. He’s excellent in an interview,” Cole said of Jordan. “He’s got boundless energy and determination.”.

Jordan’s victory means he will form a political and legal tag team with newly installed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller in pushing back on a number of investigations House Democrats have planned for President Donald Trump, some of his second-term administration officials and his business-minded family members.

In a recent development, democrats will have more than 250 seats in the chamber, with a number of races still uncalled. Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries of New York, expected to become the next House speaker, told reporters last week he predicts Democrats will have at least 255 seats when all the ballots have been counted and verification processes have played out.

“It’s a historic majority in the 21st century,” Jeffries told reporters in Washington, D.C., the day after the midterms. “The American people have chosen the economy over extremism. The American people have chosen hope over hatred. The American people have chosen common sense over corruption, chaos and cruelty. The American people have chosen House Democrats because they want to see a dramatic change in direction.”.

Political analysts have predicted an internal battle within the GOP for the direction the party takes over the next two years — and after Trump leaves office in January 2029.

Industry observers note that the Institute for Legislative Analysis, a nonprofit organization that advocates to shrink the size and influence of the government, released a vote study assessment on Monday. Its calculations led ILA to endorse Emmer and three fresh faces: Jordan, Steube and Jack.

Industry observers note that “It’s clear many Republican voters feel their representatives in Washington aren’t representing them,” Ryan McGowan, the institute’s CEO, stated in a statement. “It will be interesting to see whether House Republicans respond by choosing leaders … whose voting records are much more closely aligned with the party’s conservative base.”.

In a recent development, several GOP sources late last week, granted anonymity to be candid, said they were expecting a close outcome between Scalise and Jordan, adding Emmer was working the phones hard to remain whip. One said having either Scalise or Jordan atop the conference, with the expectation of Emmer staying on as whip, “won’t be much of a change at the top.”.

Recent findings suggest that the new leadership team will take over Jan. 3, when Democrats are expected to, in part, use their large majority to target all things Trump 2.0. The same GOP source remarked the majority party will “inevitably be pursuing impeachment by August recess despite their disciplined statements to the media pre-election.”.

Trump replied in the affirmative when a “60 Minutes” correspondent asked him in an interview that aired Sunday night if he could work with Democrats, should they also be aggressively investigating his team.

Recent findings suggest that “Well, I did it for four years,” the president mentioned of his first term. “They impeached me twice. And there are those that say that worked out to my advantage.”.

Nina Heller, Michael Macagnone and Samantha Freeman contributed to this report.

Princess Cruises is extending its Princess Plus and Princess Premier package benefits ashore, making them available at Celebration Key next year.

The packages bringing 50 to 70 percent savings per day and guest on things like drinks, dining and Wi-Fi will apply to participating locations throughout Celebration Key beginning February 1, 2027, according to a statement.
