But what about the redemption of points?

It has been revealed that well, if my first Chase Sapphire Reserve redemption is any indicator, this card may single handedly change the redemption game and just about everyone should take note — including airline and hotel transfer partners. It’s already a huge win.

Chase Travel’s ‘The Edit’ is a curated selection of nice hotels, which offer benefits similar to those provided by a travel agent or other luxury credit card booking platform. When booking a ‘The Edit’ property, you can expect breakfast for two, a $100 F&B credit, late check out and an upgrade subject to availability.

It has been revealed that which leads me to the vital bit! With the revamped Sapphire Reserve Card, there’s a new “Points Boost” feature, which offers up to two cents per point (25,000 points would cover $500, etc) for some flight or hotel purchases.

This can be amazing value, with flights of $3,000 being grabbed for just 150,000 points, with no taxes and fees and the ability to still earn frequent flyer miles and elite status points, since the airline treats it like a cash ticket.

According to recent reports, previously, the Sapphire Reserve card offered a steady point redemption opportunity directly on Chase Travel at 1.5 cents per point (100,000 points would cover $1500, etc). But with the new version, some travel purchases you want to redeem for will either offer less value than before, the same, or more, with this new ‘Points Boost’ at 2 cents per point. We like more!

I am in New York and wanted to do a little staycation, so I fired up Chase Travel and found one of my more reliable upper mid-scale hotels, The Thompson Central Park was on as part of ‘The Edit’. My two options became a very clear singular, third option.

It has been revealed that typically, I’d consider paying cash or transferring my points from Chase to Hyatt to pay for a stay like this. Hyatt has “fixed” points rates, meaning the points price is largely irrespective of the cash price and only changes by seasonal dates. For this season, it was 25,000 points per night for the Thompson Central Park.

If I were to transfer my points, I’d get a free night (the cash rate was around $500) and have a really solid points redemption at exactly two cents per point. I’m not loyal to any hotel chain really, so I wouldn’t get any breakfast or “elite” benefits, but a free night is a free night.

BUT — Chase Travel had a ‘Points Boost’ option to book the hotel directly on their platform and not transfer points to Hyatt. Chase Travel was offering this property for circa 25,000 points and that would cover the $500 cash rate, but unlike transferring points to Hyatt, because I was redeeming a ‘The Edit’ property on Chase Travel, I’d receive….

Yep, by NOT transferring my points (and dealing with the fractured transfer journey) I was able to get myself basically $200 in additional value added to my stay with the breakfast and $100 property credit, not factoring in the value of late check out or a category room upgrade. In addition, I’ll be able to earn elite nights and Hyatt Points on the stay.

Recent findings suggest that A mere 25,000 Chase Ultimate Rewards Points got me a “free” $500 hotel night, breakfast for two, and $100 to spend at the hotel. That’s a pretty stunning redemption, giving more than two cents per point of value and still allowing me to earn on the stay, unlike when you transfer your points to a loyalty program. I wish I could’ve stayed longer.

For the first time I can remember, transferring points to Hyatt was not the best option here and that’s something to stand up and take notice of.

It has been revealed that if Chase can keep up this Points Boost game, it can really send ripples through rewards. For the first time, people can easily receive tremendous value for their points through a credit card portal while still earning elite status and points with the hotel or airline of their choosing.

Sources indicate that you can check out the new 100,000 point + 500 travel credit offer for the Sapphire Reserve. It’s 200,000 points for Sapphire Reserve Business Cards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

TAP Air Portugal will launch a new route to Washington, D.C., next year.

According to recent reports, starting March 30, 2027, the carrier will connect Porto and Washington Dulles. Flights will operate three times weekly.

Currently, TAP serves Dulles from its hub at Humberto Delgado Airport in Lisbon. Its only U.S.-bound routes from Porto are to Boston and Newark, New Jersey.

TAP officials mentioned the upcoming connection will strengthen the airline’s presence in northern Portugal while expanding access to a vital foreign market.

TAP serves Porto via Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport.

The carrier serves nine destinations in the U.S., the others being New York-JFK, Chicago O’Hare, Orlando, Florida, Miami, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A new-hire Delta Air Lines pilot reportedly answered his cellphone while taxiing for departure, prompting the captain to return to the gate and have him removed.
  • The story comes from the Black Box Aviation Podcast, which recently discussed distractions on the flight deck and the consequences of using personal phones while working.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new-hire Delta Air Lines pilot reportedly answered his cellphone while taxiing for departure, prompting the captain to return to the gate and have him removed. According to an account shared on the Black Box Aviation Podcast, the first officer subsequently lost his job. If accurate, this was a remarkably poor way to begin an airline career at Delta!

The story comes from the Black Box Aviation Podcast, which recently discussed distractions on the flight deck and the consequences of using personal phones while working.

According to recent reports, according to the account, a Delta first officer was undergoing Initial Operating Experience, or IOE, when he answered his cellphone while the aircraft was taxiing for departure. Rather than continue to the runway, the captain returned to the gate. The first officer was removed and reportedly fired.

IOE involves flying actual airline trips under the supervision of a check pilot. A latest hire may have substantial flying experience elsewhere, but is still learning how to apply the new airline’s procedures in everyday operations.

New-hire FO. First trip on the line. Taxiing out in Atlanta… and his phone rings. 📵Silence it? Nope. He ANSWERED it. 🤦‍♂️Captain went back to the gate, and that was the end of his dream job.🎧 Watch the full episode in the comments 👇#PilotLife #AirlinePilot #AvGeek pic.twitter.com/QefwSoTBiN.

— The Blackbox Podcast (@the_black_box01) November 17, 2026.

There are limitations to this account. I have not obtained confirmation from Delta (understandably, no response). Furthermore, no flight number or date was referenced, so the recent discussion does not necessarily imply that this just happened. The reported dismissal should be understood as the podcast’s account…and incidents like this have been part of airline pilot lore in online forums for many years.

I suspect some passengers might hear this story and think firing someone over a phone call sounds excessive. After all, the airplane was still on the ground.

But taxiing requires the attention of both pilots. A captain may be steering, but the first officer still has work to do, including monitoring the aircraft’s progress and air traffic control instructions. A wrong turn or missed runway instruction can have very serious consequences…being a pilot is one of the professions that leaves no room for error.

Recent findings suggest that the federal sterile cockpit rule specifically includes taxi among the critical phases of flight. It prohibits activities that could distract flight crew members from their duties.

Sources indicate that A separate provision restricts the use of personal wireless communications devices at a flight crew duty station during flight, with exceptions for specified purposes under approved airline procedures. The FAA’s guidance makes clear that prohibited personal use includes telephone conversations, texting, and browsing the internet.

Pilots can use approved electronic flight bags (EFBs are the iPads that replace paper manuals and charts) and make necessary operational communications. Taking an ordinary personal call while taxiing is another matter.

In a recent development, I spend far too much time on my phone, as my weekly screen time reports reminds me every Sunday morning. I understand how reflexively we reach for it when it rings or lights up. But there are times when it simply needs to remain put away, and working in the cockpit of a moving passenger jet is certainly one of them.

What strikes me about this account is the setting. This was reportedly a upcoming hire being supervised during training. That should be a time to demonstrate that you understand the procedures and can be trusted to follow them!

According to recent reports, if the account is complete and the call was personal, I understand why the captain would have concerns about continuing the flight with that first officer. Returning to the gate would inconvenience passengers, but I would rather be delayed than have a captain continue after losing confidence in the person beside him.

According to recent reports, the employment decision is harder to assess without the full record. We do not know whether there were previous concerns or what explanation the first officer offered. I tend to be more forgiving and don’t think that every mistake during training should end a career. Even so, this would be a serious lapse in judgment. A pilot arriving at Delta should already understand why answering a personal call during taxi is unacceptable.

The Black Box Aviation Podcast recounts a Delta new-hire first officer answering his cellphone during taxi, being removed after a return to the gate, and subsequently losing his job. The incident remains unconfirmed beyond that account.

If it happened as described, I understand the captain’s decision. Passengers should be able to expect both pilots to give their attention to operating the aircraft safely. Answering personal phone call is unacceptable.

  • On November 17, Türkiye's president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed a decision to enact a latest foreign investor visa.
  • In a recent development, as for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension blueprint, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that türkiye is one of the world’s most visited countries, straddling the vibrant crossroads of Europe, Asia, and the Middle East. With sun-soaked Mediterranean beaches, Ottoman-influenced gastronomy, historic mosques, and bustling bazaars, it’s no surprise that the country attracted nearly 64 million visitors in 2025. But if your love of the country has you considering a prolonged vacation (or perhaps a second home), the government’s new golden visa might be a good fit—so long as you have $150,000 to spend.

On November 17, Türkiye's president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed a decision to enact a latest foreign investor visa. The program offers two pathways: a $150,000 investment for a three-year residence permit, or $200,000 for a five-year stay (both of which can extend to the applicant’s spouse and dependents).

In a recent development, as for where your money goes, you can deposit your funds in a local bank, buy government debt instruments, contribute to a pension blueprint, or invest in real estate or venture capital funds. No matter which pathway you select, you must hold your investment for at least half the visa term (as in, 1.5 years for the three-year visa or 2.5 years for the five-year visa). That means you could potentially withdraw your investment as early as after 18 months, according to IMI Daily, an investment migration trade publication.

The president’s announcement doesn't detail when or how foreigners can begin to apply, or the specific documents required. However, applications for the country’s other residence-by-investment permits require documents such as proof of financial means and health insurance, according to the government’s Investment and Finance Office.

If you don’t want to shell out $150,000, Türkiye offers other (renewable) relocation pathways. You may qualify for a two-year Short-Term Residence Permit for reasons such as tourism and university-sponsored research. Or, if your spouse is Turkish, you could apply for the three-year Family Residence Permit. Once you’ve lived in the country continuously for eight years, you’ll be eligible to apply for the indefinite Long-Term Residence Permit, which grants you almost all the same perks as citizenship, minus civic duties such as the ability to vote and mandatory military service.

It's important to note that the new golden visa does not provide permanent citizenship. If you’re hoping to find your way into a passport, get ready to spend more. Türkiye’s citizenship-by-investment pipeline will require you to buy a home worth at least $400,000, invest at least $500,000 in sectors such as government bonds or venture capital funds, or, alternatively, help create at least 50 jobs.

Over the last few years, the influx of latest residency-by-investment programs has made it easier for wealthy travelers to relocate internationally. In New Zealand, you can invest $1 million New Zealand Dollars (about $567,300) in exchange for a three-year work-to-residency track. For Mediterranean living, Greece offers a five-year permit for a 250,000 euro (about $291,120) investment in a startup. Or, for a more affordable option, Paraguay has a permanent residency program for those who can invest $150,000 in “tourism projects” or $200,000 in stocks or real estate—putting it in line with Türkiye as one of the more affordable relocation options.

The two carriers announced a new interline partnership that will allow travelers to combine flights on both airlines under a single ticket.

The agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S. The partnership will provide connections through French Bee’s three U.S. gateway airports that Southwest also serves: Los Angeles, Miami, and San Francisco.

French Bee also flies to Newark, Upcoming Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.

Passengers will be able to connect between French Bee’s international flights and Southwest domestic flights without having to purchase separate tickets for each airline or recheck bags at each airline.

Industry observers note that for French Bee customers, the new arrangement provides access to a much larger network of domestic destinations throughout the U.S. Southwest’s network includes cities such as Las Vegas, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Nashville, Austin, San Diego, Phoenix, and multiple destinations in the Hawaiian Islands.

The agreement represents another step in Southwest’s expanding international connectivity strategy, as the airline continues to develop relationships with overseas carriers rather than rely exclusively on its own international operations with its all-Boeing 737 fleet.

Trump says no Iran deal needed after conflict drove GOP’s midterm losses

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (762 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that president Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a Wednesday ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery in honor of Veterans Day.
  • President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.
  • Sources indicate that the possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that president Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance salute during a Wednesday ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery in honor of Veterans Day. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images).

President Donald Trump on Thursday shut down his administration’s on-again-off-again talks with Iran, saying he would not seek a deal to formally end the nine-month-old conflict with Tehran.

Sources indicate that the possible end of the pursuit of a diplomatic solution came nine days after Trump and congressional Republicans suffered massive losses in the midterm elections. House Democrats will have more than 250 seats come January, and Senate Democrats will have at least 55 seats in the Senate — with Alaska’s competitive race still uncalled.

Polls leading up to Election Day and since have shown that a majority of voters, and a sizeable chunk of Trump’s Republican base, felt the Iran conflict was a mistake.

Vice President JD Vance penned a lengthy social media post the day after the election, blaming, in large part, the Iran war for the coast-to-coast Democratic victories. Some GOP lawmakers have also called for an end to the conflict, which drove up fuel and other commodity prices.

"The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote the morning after the GOP wipeout. "The president himself said so last night.".

Industry observers note that trump has said that he agrees with Vance’s assessment but that if he had to decide again whether to join Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in striking Iranian targets, he would reach the same conclusion. On Monday, he told reporters that the Iran war "militarily is effectively over.".

Vance had been Trump’s designated top negotiator in the talks with Iran’s remaining leaders, but the president noted Thursday on social media that he had ordered his second-in-command to instead “focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.”.

In a recent development, “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed,” he added. “We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!".

It has been revealed that the situation along the Strait of Hormuz remains contested and dangerous for commercial vessels, including ones that deliver a large amount of the world’s oil products. Iranian officials contend that they control most of the key waterway.

It has been revealed that trump, Vance and other administration officials have stated in recent weeks that they were open to continuing talks with Iran, while criticizing Tehran's negotiating tactics. Last week, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who also is Trump’s national security adviser, told reporters that Iran's latest demands were unreasonable.

It has been revealed that trump’s announcement Thursday could represent his latest way to try assuaging GOP voters, including members of his “Make America Great Again” base. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after the midterms and released Tuesday highlighted that a majority of Republicans (51 percent) want Congress to pass legislation that would end the Iran conflict. Overall, 71 percent of Americans would support such a bill, the survey found.

The conflict was front-and-center during the midterms campaign.

Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers, who lost the Senate race in Michigan to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, called for the Iran conflict to end "rapidly.".

“Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life. Groceries cost too much. We have to bring prices down," Rogers remarked in one campaign ad.

On Capitol Hill, GOP lawmakers have tried giving Trump cover, while raising some concerns about high gas prices and questioning whether the president and his team have a viable exit strategy.

In a recent development, as the midterms campaign hit the homestretch in late September, two Iowa Republicans in tight races, Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks, voted with Democrats on a measure to end the conflict.

“With the negotiating window closed, sustained combat operations now require congressional authorization,” Nunn, an Air Force veteran, wrote on social media. “I will not support another open-ended war.”.

Nunn and Miller-Meeks both lost their seats last week, despite breaking with the president over the war.

Trump’s declaration this week of a military end to the Iran war came more than seven years after he offered some foreshadowing during a June 25, 2019, exchange with this CQ Roll Call reporter in the Oval Office.

In a recent development, asked that day what his exit strategy would be if war ever broke out with Iran, he said: “You’re not going to need an exit strategy. I don’t do exit strategies.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lufthansa Group aims to lay off around 1,000 full-time workers at its flagship carrier as elevated fuel prices and service disruptions continue to undercut earnings.

In a recent development, the airline group disclosed the cuts in a letter sent to employees and seen by Dow Jones Newswire, according to The Wall Street Journal. The reductions will target Lufthansa’s hubs in Frankfurt and Munich.

Tech giant leaders said their 2024 turnaround plan, initially expected to boost earnings by €2.5 billion over four years, is no longer enough to keep the brand on solid financial ground.

“The year 2026 has set us back: the war in the Middle East, the still very high fuel costs, nine days of strike action, and our already very high cost base have intensified the situation,” the letter said.

Lufthansa failed to reach an agreement with its pilot union earlier this week, setting the stage for a possible work stoppage. The impasse has already resulted in two short strikes, one in February, the other in March.

In a recent development, lufthansa Group has spoken openly about the damage caused by higher fuel prices over the last nine months. Over the summer, it retired aircraft, cut routes, and warned that layoffs were likely unless prices eased.

According to EuroNews, Lufthansa has lost on average about €20 million per month since the start of the year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that former Maine Gov.
  • Paul LePage, the former Maine governor who once stated he was “Donald Trump before Donald Trump,” is heading to Congress.
  • The Associated Press called the race for the open 2nd District on Thursday after the Maine Secretary of State’s office tabulated the votes under the state’s ranked choice voting system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, fifth from right, joins incoming members Thursday for their freshman class photo on the House steps outside the Capitol. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Paul LePage, the former Maine governor who once stated he was “Donald Trump before Donald Trump,” is heading to Congress.

The Associated Press called the race for the open 2nd District on Thursday after the Maine Secretary of State’s office tabulated the votes under the state’s ranked choice voting system. LePage ended up ahead of Democratic state Auditor Matt Dunlap 50.8 percent to 49.2 percent.

Sources indicate that dunlap had already conceded the race to LePage, who will succeed retiring Democratic Rep. Jared Golden in the sprawling district, which includes much of Maine outside the Portland and Augusta areas.

“Paul LePage is already hard at work for the people of Maine attending Congressional orientation, meeting with national leaders, and making it clear the political parties need to work together for the American people,” Brent Littlefield, a senior adviser to LePage, noted in a statement Thursday. “As Paul said, he will work with anyone, regardless of Party, to put Maine first.”.

Sources indicate that lePage’s win is a glimmer of good news for Republicans, who saw massive losses across the country in last week’s midterm elections. He is one of three Republicans, along with Texas’ Jace Yarbrough and Tennessee’s Brent Taylor, to have flipped a House seat, although Maine’s 2nd District is the only one of the three that wasn’t redrawn to favor the GOP.

LePage’s win also means that at least one Republican will continue to represent New England in Congress, taking up the mantle from Maine Sen. Susan Collins, who lost her own reelection bid last week.

Golden, who was first elected in 2018, had been a top Republican target throughout his time in Congress. But the lawmaker, known for bucking his party, proved difficult to unseat in the past two election cycles.

“I also know a thing or two about winning in tough circumstances. So, I know you have to tip your hat to Paul LePage for winning in the midst of this Blue Tsunami,” Golden said in a social media post last week.

In a recent development, dunlap initially debuted his campaign as a primary challenge to Golden in the fall of 2025, only for the congressman to announce his retirement a month later. Dunlap went on to win a four-way contest for the Democratic nomination.

At the Races: Regional realignment

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.
  • Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout.
  • It has been revealed that one Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New England is the ancestral home of moderate Republicans, from the Saltonstalls to the Bushes, whose fiscal conservatism and social moderation defined the national GOP for decades.

Last week, Yankee Republicans suffered a near-total wipeout. Maine’s Susan Collins, Latest England's last GOP senator, lost her seat to Democrat Troy Jackson, leaving former Maine Gov. Paul LePage, who just won a House seat, as the lone Republican headed to Congress from the region. (The picture was a bit brighter at the state level, where GOP Govs. Phil Scott of Vermont and Kelly Ayotte of New Hampshire were both reelected.).

It has been revealed that one Republican operative sees a path out of the wilderness in a post-Trump era. In an opinion piece in The Boston Globe, consultant Kristin Tate urged New England Republicans to focus on fiscal discipline and recognize that “independence from national party leadership can be a political asset, not an act of betrayal.”.

After all, as the midterm election results remind us, no political realignment lasts forever.

Three decades ago, there were plenty of moderate Democrats from Southern states serving in Congress, governor’s mansions and even the White House. But in the years since Bill Clinton's exit from the political stage, Democrats have largely written off the South.

Which is partly why last week’s Democratic wins in the Carolinas, Georgia and, perhaps most notably, Mississippi were so stunning. All the elements that powered the party to victory nationally – disillusionment with Donald Trump, a rise in economic populism and hunger for change – played a role in the South as well.

But other factors were unique to a region that has seen renewed attempts to dilute Black political power with the redrawing of House districts to favor the GOP.

The Republican redistricting gambit in Southern states did not fully yield the desired results and seems to have helped galvanize Black voters and their allies, powering Democrats to unlikely victories.

It’s too soon to say whether the GOP’s reduced hold on the South represents a temporary blip or an enduring shift.

But Joe Trippi, a longtime Democratic strategist who advised candidates in Alabama and Florida this year, has a message for his party: “We need to invest in the South.”.

In a recent development, #MSSEN: Democrat Scott Colom defeated GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction and the first in his party to win a Senate seat in the Magnolia State since 1982.

Tar Heel tidal wave: Democrats in North Carolina have picked up at least five House seats, a striking development given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Prior to last week, no House Republican incumbent had lost a general election in the state since Republicans won control of the redistricting process more than a decade ago. And the Democratic gains could grow: In the 5th District, former journalist Chuck Hubbard narrowly leads 11-term Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx, and in the 3rd District, former state Rep. Raymond Smith holds a razor-thin edge over Republican Rep. Greg Murphy. The Associated Press had not called either race at publication time, though Murphy has conceded.

Republicans pick campaign chairs: Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno and Georgia Rep. Brian Jack will be the chairs of Republicans’ respective campaign committees for the 2028 cycle. GOP lawmakers held their leadership elections Tuesday, as our colleagues Savannah Behrmann and John T. Bennett reported. Senate Republicans are sticking with South Dakota’s John Thune to lead them in the next Congress, while House Republicans picked former Freedom Caucus Chair Jim Jordan as their leader.

Redistricting doubts: Maryland could be getting a newly introduced congressional map after voters approved a constitutional amendment that would clear the way for new lines in 2028. Our colleague Victor Feldman has more on the result and other election-related ballot measures across the country. But it’s not clear how many other states may look to redistrict next cycle after Republican efforts over the past 18 months largely didn’t pay off in last week’s elections.

Recent findings suggest that run the table: With Rep. Darren Soto winning a sixth term in Florida, no Democratic incumbent lost reelection to a Republican this year. Soto’s win in a redrawn district also meant that Florida Democrats defended all four seats the GOP had targeted under a upcoming congressional map.

California contest: Rep. Ken Calvert defeated fellow Republican Rep. Young Kim in a rare member-versus-member contest for a redrawn Southern California seat that turned acrimonious. Republicans are poised to hold just four House seats in the Golden State after Democrats made good on five pickup opportunities under a new congressional map.

Cheesecake Factory caucus: The latest episode of the Political Theater podcast, hosted by Roll Call editor-in-chief Jason Dick, breaks down how candidates in both parties fared in counties where The Cheesecake Factory operates, after the popular chain restaurant became something of a side character in the closing weeks of the midterm campaign.

Back to school: Newly elected members of Congress are on Capitol Hill this week for freshman orientation, an experience Massachusetts Rep.-elect Dan Koh told our colleague Nina Heller is “like high school – but it’s fun high school.” The incoming lawmakers took their class photo Thursday morning and will get to pick their Capitol Hill offices after next week’s famed lottery, Nina writes.

Tracking the count: As of 4:30 p.m. Eastern time Thursday, House Democrats had flipped 44 seats, while Republicans had picked up three. Twelve races remain uncalled, including a pair in Louisiana that will be decided by December runoffs. On the Senate side, Democrats have flipped eight seats, with only Alaska’s race still undecided.

Guv upgrade: Democrats flipped at least five governorships last week and will hold a majority of governor’s mansions next year. Two gubernatorial races remain uncalled by the AP: Kansas, where Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher is narrowly ahead of Republican state Senate President Ty Masterson, and Alaska, where Democratic former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins is just below the 50 percent threshold to win the election outright. In territorial elections, Republicans flipped the governor’s office in Guam while voters in the Northern Mariana Islands will pick their next governor in a Nov. 20 runoff.

Industry observers note that #TNSEN: Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn, who was elected Tennessee governor last week, is poised to pick her Senate successor. According to the Nashville Banner, the short list includes Knox County Mayor Glenn Jacobs, a former professional wrestler, Reps. Tim Burchett and Chuck Fleischmann, and Tennessee Deputy Gov. Stuart McWhorter.

2028 on the brain: A handful of House Democrats are already considering 2028 Senate bids, according to Axios, including Kansas’ Sharice Davids, North Carolina’s Don Davis and Pennsylvania’s Chris DeLuzio.

Recent findings suggest that senator Morrison? Minnesota Rep. Kelly Morrison is earning buzz as a potential appointee to fill the Senate seat that Democrat Amy Klobuchar is vacating to become governor, Semafor reports. House Democrats aren’t likely to be as concerned about open seats as their Republican counterparts were in recent years, given the size of the incoming Democratic majority.

AOC’s future: Progressive activists have released a latest organization to encourage New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. Meanwhile, Axios reports that Ocasio-Cortez has parted ways with the digital fundraising firm she’s worked with for several years and has brought on the same firm that Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders used during his two presidential campaigns.

Women lead: Shirley Emehelu is New Jersey’s new lieutenant governor after Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill picked her to succeed Dale Caldwell, who resigned in September amid sexual harassment allegations and other ethical lapses. New Jersey is now one of five states to have women in both the governor’s and lieutenant governor’s offices, along with Massachusetts, Arkansas, Iowa and Virginia. Iowa will come off the list next year after an all-male Democratic ticket swept this year’s gubernatorial race, though five other states elected women to both offices last week.

Sources indicate that congress will once again be filled with losers – i.e, fresh members who have lost previous bids for elected office. Roll Call elections analyst Nathan L. Gonzales of Inside Elections returns to his biennial tradition as he runs down the latest list of “losers.”.

Ducking the wave: Democrats notched major wins in unexpected places, but one state grew redder after last week’s elections. The New York Times checks in with voters in South Dakota, where the GOP won all nine statewide elections.

Here come the MBAs: Democrats with corporate connections were among the winners in last week’s elections, countering the idea that candidates with serious business credentials have struggled within the party, The Wall Street Journal reports. The field of 19 winners with M.B.A. degrees includes Costco board member Helena Buonanno Foulkes, who won the Rhode Island governor’s race, and Paige Cognetti, a Goldman Sachs alum who flipped a House seat in Pennsylvania.

How Ricketts did it: Nebraska Sen. Pete Ricketts’ election night success was one of the few bright spots for the GOP. Ricketts fended off a challenge from independent Dan Osborn by painting him as a Democrat, questioning his authenticity and highlighting leaked audio of his comments denigrating Trump voters, writes the Nebraska Examiner.

According to recent reports, was it necessary? California redrew its congressional map to favor Democrats in response to Texas taking a similar step to boost the GOP. But some are questioning whether the state needed to cast aside its independent redistricting commission to rejigger the lines, given the scale of Democrats’ wins. “What they were literally saying is, ‘Let’s undo democracy to protect democracy,’” Lincoln Project co-founder Mike Madrid told CalMatters. “There’s something very Orwellian about it.”.

Song of the cycle: The New York Times reviews “Talafreako,” an unlikely viral anthem celebrating the newly elected Democratic senator from Texas.

History does rhyme: An opinion piece in The (Charleston) Post & Courier argues that the win by Democratic Sen.-elect Annie Andrews is the latest in a long line of cases in which South Carolina voters bucked the idea of party bosses picking their leaders.

The man behind the grill: The Fresh York Times profiles Russ Hudson, the Mississippi man in Colom’s now-legendary “Pick another protein” ad.

That was the last time Democrats won 11 House seats in North Carolina.

As of Thursday afternoon, they appear on track to match that number. They’ve already won nine seats – a mark they last cleared in the 1982 midterms – and they’re narrowly ahead in two more races.

Sources indicate that if those leads hold, Democrats' 11-member delegation would look much different than the one sworn in some 66 years ago in 1961. Tar Heel Democrats taking office in January would include four women, six Black members and one Hispanic member.

Their 11 representatives (out of 12) in the 87th Congress were all white men who consistently voted to uphold racial segregation and oppose major federal civil rights legislation.

Vote counting in Alaska is expected to conclude by Wednesday, Nov. 18, the targeted date for ranked choice tabulations in races in which no candidate took more than 50 percent of the vote. As of Thursday, Democratic former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in the Senate race, though she’s below the 50 percent threshold.

Meanwhile, Democrats are gathering in Denver beginning Thursday to celebrate their historic wins and plot their next steps.

    Where Was 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Filmed? Behind the Scenes in Spain and Germany

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more.
    • Industry observers note that we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens.
    • Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that on Location peels back the curtain on some of your favorite films, television shows, and more. This time, we take a look at The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Industry observers note that we’re heading back to Panem for the sixth time this autumn, as the latest Hunger Games prequel hits screens. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the action of the first film and tells the origin story of Katniss Everdeen’s grumpy tutor, Haymitch Abernathy, as he enters the Games himself.

    Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.

    Based on the books by Suzanne Collins, the dystopian series is set in a futuristic America in which each district must send a teenage tribute to fight to the death in an annual competition—the idea being that, by doing so, the public will be too afraid to rebel against President Snow.

    Recent findings suggest that this edition of the games is known as the Quarter Quell, with double the number of tributes being sent into the arena, meaning the stakes are so much higher. Interest in the film is high, not least because Haymitch is so beloved in the original series, portrayed by Woody Harrelson. Newcomer Joseph Zada takes the lead role in the latest film, while Hollywood heavyweights Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, and Kieran Culkin also star.

    One of the most key sets in the film is the arena where the games take place, and for this, director Francis Lawrence opted not for CGI and a green screen, but instead a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in northern Spain. Below, we look into the locations used in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Ben Wang as Wyatt Callow, Percy Daggs IV as Ampert Latier, Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Sources indicate that within the book and film series, the settings for the Hunger Games are always known to be virtually spectacular. For this film, filmmakers settled on the vast and untouched landscape of Somiedo Natural Park in the Asturias region of northern Spain, which boasts mountain ranges, glacial valleys, beautiful meadows, dense forests, and tranquil lakes. The remote region is also home to the last brown bear population in Europe.

    Sources indicate that when the tributes are rolled out into the arena, they are presented with a vast Cornucopia, a pile of weapons, food, and other supplies that might be useful to them in the competition. These scenes were filmed at Somiedo Natural Park, with the Asturian mountains and a glacial lake in the background.

    “Somiedo is a spectacular place,” noted Pedro Aráez, supervising location manager. “The valleys, forests, and mountains have a very wild, untouched feeling, which was exactly what the filmmakers were looking for. It’s remote, dramatic, and visually unique. When you arrive there, you immediately understand why it was chosen.”.

    Recent findings suggest that located close to Somiedo, the Teverga beech forest, Hayedo de Montegrande, was used for some of the dense woodland scenes, in which contestants battle it out and hide in the woods. Other scenes filmed here utilized a series of glacial lakes, the Saliencia Lakes and the Lago de la Cueva.

    Iris Apatow as Proserpina Trinket and Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Before the tributes are released into the arena, they are first held in special little pods underground which are arranged in a circle around the Cornucopia. The perfect location for this? A velodrome, of course, which is steeply circular so cyclists can race around it. The film crew utilized Berlin’s Velodrom for this very purpose, with its cold, clinical silver decor perfect for matching the hi-tech aesthetic associated with the Capitol.

    Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.

    According to recent reports, prior to entering the Games, tributes must introduce themselves on the public stage, during a televised grand chariot parade in the Capitol. Another Berlin location with links to the sporting world was used for this purpose: the Olympiastadion. For fans of the earlier films, this is the moment when Jennifer Lawrence’s character Katniss becomes “the girl on fire” with her incredible flaming dress.

    The futuristic architecture of Edificio Calatrava in Oviedo, Spain—with its striking, claw-like structure—stands in for a building in the Capitol, where President Snow and his government live. The complex was designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, whose work is known for resembling living organisms. Meanwhile, the 14th-century Ehreshoven Castle, just outside of Cologne, was also used as a filming location, with local press reporting that its lush interiors might have been used to stand in for somewhere inside the Capitol.

    A former smelting factory complex in western Germany, Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord provides the backdrop for one of the most atmospheric settings in the films, Haymitch’s home of District 12. The vast complex is able to stand in for multiple places within the district, a former mining town that has fallen on seriously bad times. Rather than being a desolate area stumbled upon by the filmmakers, Landschaftspark is popular for its nightly light installation by British artist Jonathan Park. There are also regular al fresco events here, from film screenings to the annual art-meets-sport Ruhr Games and Traumzeit Festival. Another location in Germany, Lindlar Quarry, was used for District 12, with wooden huts built here to resemble the outskirts of the village.

    • A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.
    • Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

    Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., stated Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

    According to recent reports, “I know it’s going to be my main push,” he said. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

    Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

    In a recent development, “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators stated. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

    It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

    House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., said earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

    According to recent reports, while ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the new Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

    But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how promptly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

    Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, said that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

    She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

    Democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., noted Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

    Sources indicate that "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries said.

    It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro noted earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

    The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

    Recent findings suggest that the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks said. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

    Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home. Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, pair timeless charm with an ease you'll never find stateside. Here, you can sip Champagne in front of Sleeping Beauty's castle—or visit a dragon beneath it—while filling your days with delightful architecture, unprecedented thrills, and the wildest wilderness ride Disney's ever built (Big Thunder Mountain!).

    Industry observers note that there's also never been a better time to visit. Walt Disney Studios Park's March 2026 transformation into the latest Disney Adventure World brought a drone-filled nighttime show, Avengers coaster, and even a Frozen-themed land featuring a lifelike Olaf robot to its once-faltering second gate. Now, between Fantasyland classics and futuristic favorites, there's something new and thrilling for the entire family to experience.

    Of course, you'll need somewhere to rest your head at night, and that's where the best hotels near Disneyland Paris come into play. Staying at a Disney-branded property typically affords guests special amenities including ticket packages, exclusive character meet-and-greets, and Extra Magic Time, which provides bonus time in the parks prior to opening. These hotels are great options, but can also be pricey—luckily, there are also a few non-branded properties in the area that make for great alternatives. There's something here for everyone and every budget.

    Unsure of whether you want to add something so Américain to your Paris vacation? As a theme park journalist who has visited all Disney parks worldwide, trust me: It's worth the visit. Even with so many cultural monuments in Paris, nothing is more delightfully uncanny than witnessing the United States section of It's a Small World. So, whether you're looking for glamour or simply a good location, read on for the very best hotels near Disneyland Paris.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Three-minute walk.

    It has been revealed that as the crown jewel of France's Disney resort, this 487-room property is Disney's best hotel overseas—and, quite possibly, in the entire world. After undergoing an extensive three-year overhaul, the iconic pink palace reopened in 2024 with princess suites and luxurious amenities worthy of its five-star ranking. Great for couples or families, guests can anticipate the ultimate royal treatment thanks to rooms with romantic castle views just steps from the park. With kids treatments at the Spa by Clarins and two complimentary hours of childcare each day, parents can unwind at the Fleur de Lys bar, enjoy a prix fixe meal at chef Jean Imbert's on-site restaurant, or perhaps even sneak back into the parks themselves. (We won't tell.).

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Eight-minute drive.

    Industry observers note that rustic-chic in the best of ways, Marriott's Village d'Île-de-France offers cozy abodes that sleep up to eight with full kitchens, washing machines, and plenty of space to stretch out, all a short shuttle ride from the theme parks. Designed to emulate the charms of a small Parisian village, these quaint studios and multi-bedroom town houses feel more like cottages than traditional vacation rentals. Surroundings like these may sound quotidien to someone like Princess Belle, but the resort is as sweet as the rooms are spacious, making it an ideal choice for a hotel near Disneyland Paris as well as extended trips to nearby towns.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    Industry observers note that considering it's the only hotel in the world dedicated to Marvel's famed comic book characters, it's no surprise the Infinity Stone–colored beverages and slick, silver rooms at Disney Hotel Fresh York - The Art of Marvel are somewhat out of this world. Family-friendly amenities like superhero meet-and-greets and a design studio with character drawing experiences make it the ultimate getaway for any comic book–obsessed fan in your family. Yet, even with hundreds of unique pieces of artwork, it won't feel like you're living through an Infinity War. Delicately executed details, like Manhattan Restaurant's Asgard-inspired chandelier and Spider-Man swinging across the panel screens at Skyline Bar, provide simple city elegance with the lightest touch of Marvel magic.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 17-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    If this hotel reminds you of Walt Disney World's Yacht & Beach Club resorts, you're not mistaken—this 1,098-room Disneyland Paris hotel was inspired by its Florida counterpart. The nautical theming is strong, and it's that seaside charm that keeps parkgoers returning to this waterfront escape. Just a 15-minute walk from the park gates, guests can meet maritime Mickey & Minnie Mouse (who don delightful cruisewear) or indulge in a seafood buffet at the aptly named Cape Cod restaurant. It's modeled after a familiar location back in the States, sure, but after spending the day with princesses, dragons, and superheroes, you may find yourself overjoyed to return to those country club comforts.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 13-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    Craving a bit more theming on your Disneyland Paris trip? Look no further than this national park–inspired escape. It offers lodge-style living perfect for a wintertime trip. Cozy up to the Redwood Bar & Lounge hearth, or in one of the newly renovated rooms with nods to Bambi and Pocahontas, and take in the charms of what Disney does best. Multiple on-site buffets allow you to feast like you've been on the move all day because, well, you likely have.

    According to recent reports, note that this Disney-operated hotel is right now undergoing a phased refurbishment. For stays in late 2026 and early 2027, I recommend selecting a refurbished room in The Lodges. Starting in February 2027, construction will move to general hotel spaces, and certain facilities will be temporarily unavailable.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 30-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    Recent findings suggest that rooms at the boutique Hôtel l’Elysée Val d’Europe are modern and minimal, offering the perfect escape from any theme park chaos. Though it's just a 30-minute walk or a short, free shuttle ride away from the gates, the real perk of being a bit removed is its proximity to the Val d’Europe shopping complex and the designer outlet mall La Vallée Village. With a bounty of discounted prices on luxury brands like Prada, Saint Laurent, and Gucci, you're sure to find a Parisian souvenir that'll rival the array of Mickey Mouse goods sold within the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Nine-minute drive.

    In a recent development, if the City of Lights appeals to you for its style and romance, consider this your ideal hotel. Design-forward rooms with concrete walls, sleek bathrooms, and an open, plant-walled lobby offer reliable value without sacrificing taste, making it a perfect choice for travelers seeking something a little less Disney. While families will benefit from select rooms offering full kitchens and stovetops, the upgraded amenities—which include a heated indoor pool, sauna, and hammam—offer a little something for everyone, just beyond the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 16-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    In a recent development, step right up to this quirky hotel that feels like a Western film set and is jam-packed with Toy Story details. Small touches, like cowprint bedspreads and appearances by Woody and Jessie, make Disney Hotel Cheyenne a hidden gem that's nearly as themed as Disneyland Paris's own Frontierland. Given that it's significantly more affordable than the majority of its Disneyland-owned counterparts yet retains perks like Extra Magic Time, this property offers a best-of-both-worlds approach for those who want to live a full Disney-fied day from first rides to fireworks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute drive.

    Multi-room cabins at this expansive, woodsy resort are the perfect way to experience a taste of the outdoors between trips on Massive Thunder Mountain. Sadly, there are no theme park shuttle services, so parks must be reached by car, rideshare, or taxi. But that's not to say it's worth skipping—here, nature abounds in both form and function. There's an on-site aviary, comfort food at the Crockett's Tavern buffet, and plenty of rustic charm, so the comforts of home are never too far away. Consider this Disneyland Paris hotel as close as you can get to camping at Disneyland's theme parks—if camping also included unfettered access to Mickey waffles.

    What area is the best to stay in when visiting Disneyland Paris?

    Any hotel near Disney Village, the entertainment and dining district at the entrance to Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, is going to be the most convenient choice. This not only offers more ease and access, but affords you the option to shop and dine after the parks close each night. Still, booking nearly any Disney-operated hotel will give you benefits like Extra Magic Time and exclusive character encounters, which help get you even more out of your Disneyland Paris vacation.

    Are there any hotels that are walking distance to Disneyland Paris?

    Yes—but you might want to bring your sneakers. Disneyland Hotel is located directly at the entrance to Disneyland Paris, while Disney Hotel New York - The Art of Marvel, Disney Newport Bay Club, and Disney Sequoia Lodge are all a 10- to 15-minute walk through Disney Village to reach both parks. Disney Hotel Cheyenne is a further trek, about 15 to 20 minutes away, but absolutely doable. Shuttle buses are available as well.

    What is the 3-2-1 rule at Disneyland Paris?

    It has been revealed that the 3-2-1 rule is essentially shorthand for how to streamline your Disneyland Paris experience. Experts recommend selecting three rides, two entertainment offerings, and one dining option for an easy, straightforward approach to planning a day at any Disney theme park. It works as well at Walt Disney World and Disneyland as it does here at Disneyland Paris, but I recommend you still do a little research before you go. Be sure you don't skip Phantom Manor, which can only be found in Paris, secure your dining reservations early, and don't miss the nighttime indicates offered at both parks—they're among the best in the world.

    It is best to stay within the park at Disneyland Paris, or outside of it?

    According to recent reports, it goes without saying that the closer you are to the castle, the “better” your hotel will be, but it shouldn't be a deal-breaker. Convenience is always a factor, but Disney-operated hotels at Disneyland Paris tend to be much pricier than their American counterparts, so staying a bus ride away might be necessary. Still, the perks are plenty across most of Disneyland's own hotels, including extra time in the parks, which is why I recommended so many of them.

    #77068. Tech Report: A Guide to NYC’s Little Italy—and the Culinary Gems Hidden Among the Tourist Traps

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1399 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: A Guide to NYC’s Little Italy—and the Culinary Gems Hidden Among the Tourist Traps

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1399 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that contrary to other tourist-focused neighborhoods in New York (looking at you, Times Square), Little Italy boasts an innate charm that resonates with visitors and locals alike.
    • According to recent reports, A note on how we’re defining the area: Over the years, Little Italy’s boundaries have shrunk to focus on the touristic area of Mulberry Street and its immediate surroundings.
    • Located in the heart of Little Italy, Umberto’s Clam House is best known for its—you guessed it, all things clams.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that contrary to other tourist-focused neighborhoods in New York (looking at you, Times Square), Little Italy boasts an innate charm that resonates with visitors and locals alike. Sandwiched between SoHo and the Lower East Side, this jewel box area is home to long-standing, family-owned restaurants and authentic Italian bakeries, the majority of which have been neighborhood staples for decades. Yet despite its touristy atmosphere, a unique feeling of old school New York magic hangs in the air; beyond the personality-less stands and souvenir shops, framed family photos on restaurant walls and structural imperfections of tenement buildings speak to a bygone area of the city’s past, evoking a sense of nostalgia that so many neighborhoods lack. Pop down to Mulberry Street and see for yourself—though be sure you know which spots are actually legit (that’s where we come in).

    According to recent reports, A note on how we’re defining the area: Over the years, Little Italy’s boundaries have shrunk to focus on the touristic area of Mulberry Street and its immediate surroundings. While the southern and western boundaries of Canal Street and Lafayette Streets remain unchanged, the historic easterly Bowery boundary has arguably shifted to Elizabeth Street; similarly, the northerly boundary of Kenmare has also condensed down, according to many, to Broome Street. For the sake of this piece, we’re using the boundaries of Lafayette Street, Canal Street, Elizabeth Street, and Broome Street as a happy medium.

    Located in the heart of Little Italy, Umberto’s Clam House is best known for its—you guessed it, all things clams. The restaurant promptly garnered attention shortly after opening in 1972, when mobster Joe "Crazy Joe" Gallo was shot in the restaurant’s dining room. Like its mafia-related history, the food at Umberto’s is as Italian-American as it gets. Baked clams and fried calamari are the appetizer list’s biggest show-stoppers, while superbly chilled clams on the half-shell pair exquisitely with equally cold (and generously sized) cocktails from the bar. Seafood-focused mains are the name of the game here, including the garlicky linguini and clam sauce and recently resurfaced scungilli with pasta served with piping hot red sauce.

    Address: 132 Mulberry Street, New York, NY 10013.

    For Italian-American eats in a less stereotypically Little Italy ambiance, Il Cortile is the way to go. Contrary to the old school Italian vibes found in the majority of the neighborhood’s restaurants, Il Cortile’s atrium-style glass ceiling and plant-filled room feel more like dining al fresco in Trastevere than the heart of Mulberry Street. The family-owned restaurant’s neighborhood roots date back to 1975, with a solid focus on Northern Italian cuisine. The homemade cheese ravioli and wood-fired pizzas are always a safe bet, though for meat lovers, springing for the Fettuccine di Parma made with sweet sausage and wild mushrooms won’t disappoint—and be sure to save room for the pillowy soft tiramisu made with creamy mascarpone and imported Italian ladyfingers drenched in espresso.

    Address: 125 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10013.

    According to recent reports, original Vincent’s, often called The Original Vincent’s Clam Bar, is home to one of the richest restaurant success stories in Little Italy. Founded in 1904 by Giuseppe and Carmela Siano, the business began as a sidewalk street cart serving up fresh seafood and jars of homemade red sauce, available in mild, medium, and hot. Today, the restaurant sits on the corner of Mott and Hester Streets, and is still known for its signature gravies, baked clams, and linguini-based pasta dishes (don’t skip the frutti di mare). As in its earliest days, Original Vincent’s still sells jars of their red sauce to-go, making replicating the restaurant’s pasta dishes at home a breeze—simply grab a bottle of Chianti, cue up your Louis Primo playlist and voila.

    Address: 119 Mott St, Fresh York, NY 10013.

    Paesano of Mulberry Street is home to one of the coziest interiors in Little Italy, offering a peaceful refuge from the neighborhood bustle. Rustic twig bunches and leafy plants strung with twinkle lights hang from the ceiling, while traditional Italian frescos and framed family photographs adorn the whitewashed brick walls. Originally opened in 1961, the restaurant remains owned by the same family and continues to be known for their Southern Italian recipes, including linguini with clam sauce, wood-fired pizzas, and savory chicken marsala drenched in sautéed mushrooms. Meat lovers, don’t skip the restaurant’s signature Veal A La Paesano, featuring a juicy and tender veal base layered with thin slices of prosciutto, steamed broccoli, and gooey mozzarella cheese finished with succulent brown gravy.

    Address: 136 Mulberry St, Newly introduced York, NY 10013.

    For serious pizza lovers, a trip to Lombardi’s is a no-brainer. Tucked on the corner of Mott and Spring, this neighborhood institution is credited as America’s first pizzeria, originally founded by Gennaro Lombardi in 1905. Lombardi quickly rose to fame for his large, heavily-topped pies, which he baked in an on-site, coal-and-gas oven. The result? Smoky crusts topped with perfectly balanced tomato sauce and gobs of whole milk mozzarella—along with sweet Italian sausage and various other accoutrements. The interior oozes with classic Fresh York charm, featuring tables clad in red-and-white checkered cloths and framed family photographs strung along the red-hued walls. Head’s up, the spot is cash only, and while there’s an ATM on site, we recommend coming prepared to avoid the withdrawal fee.

    Address: 30 Spring St, Fresh York, NY 10012.

    Pasquale Jones-12_2. Brussels Sprout Pizza with Red Onion, Smoked Mozzarella & Lemon.

    In a sea of mediocre neighborhood wine lists, Pasqule Jones offers a breath of fresh air for Little Italy exploring wine lovers. Situated on the cusp of the neighborhood’s boundaries (and easily identifiable by its rainbow neon lights), this Italian-American pizzeria first opened its doors in 2016 and quickly became a staple for industry folks and visiting oenophiles alike. Beloved for its wood-fired New York style pizzas (don’t miss the signature clam pie) and thick, homemade pastas, the restaurant’s warm-yet-casual ambiance is ideal for posting up with a pie and a bottle—especially if you’re after great Burgundy, Champagne, or Italian reds. Expect classic picks from Pierre-Yves Colin-Morey, Domaine de l’Arlot, and Vietti, as well ample fun and fresh selections from Sandlands, Chacra, and Domaine Gramenon.

    Address: 187 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10012.

    Address: 195 Grand St, New York, NY 10013.

    In a recent development, although less famous than nearby Ferrara, Caffé Palermo features the innate Italian charm one looks for when wandering the neighborhood. Owned and operated by Baby John DeLutro (the self-proclaimed “Cannoli King”) since 1973, the establishment lives up to its owner’s moniker, offering flavored iterations—including pistachio and hazelnut made with sweet ricotta cream, the former of which is one of the joint’s standouts—in perfectly crisp shells. What Palermo does have over Ferrara is a solid amount of outdoor seating, ideal for posting up with a cappuccino and people watching on Mulberry.

    Address: 148 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10013.

    La Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels.

    If you’re looking for a wine break between pizza and pastries, this is just the ticket. Located on Little Italy's western limits (Centre Street between Broome and Grand), this French-inspired wine bar offers extensive by-the-glass options and shareable bites, including cheese and charcuterie boards to larger main courses, including beef tartare and lemon spaghetti. The comprehensive wine list, which features anywhere from 750 to 1,000+ references at all times, leans unsurprisingly French, though ample selections from Italy, Spain, and the USA are also available. Our suggestion? Post up with a bottle of Grower Champagne and relish in the perfectly executed Parisian bar à vin ambiance.

    Address: 249 Centre St, Upcoming York, NY 10013.

    Address: 409 Broome St, New York, NY 10013.

    Technically located on the cusp of Little Italy’s historic boundaries (Kenmare and Broome Streets), La Esquina offers a flavor-packed reprieve from the classic red-sauce joints synonymous with the neighborhood. Situated in a former counter deli, this multi-level Mexican hotspot is best known for its casual taqueria (located in ‘The Corner Deli’ space) serving tacos, tortas, and ceviche. However, for those looking for something a bit stronger, head through the secret door and down the stairs to find the restaurant’s underground speakeasy. Lit by candle and adorned with Lucha Libre posters, the bar’s high-energy ambiance is prime for enjoying queso fundido and smoky Mexican street corn (elotes callejeros) washed down with expertly crafted agave-based cocktails.

    Address: 114 Kenmare St, Fresh York, NY 10012.

    #77067. Industry News: American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (789 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: American officially retires its most exclusive long-haul seat: Bittersweet or overdue?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.
    • We’ve been talking for years about American’s intends to retire its international-style first-class product.
    • The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s the end of an era at American Airlines.

    This week, the carrier (officially) bid farewell to Flagship First international service.

    We’ve been talking for years about American’s intends to retire its international-style first-class product.

    The airline is replacing Flagship First with larger and more modern business-class cabins on its marquee planes — cabins that will feature its next-generation Flagship Suites.

    For a lot of flyers, that’s likely to be a positive shift: It will mean a host of upgrades in business-class, including seats with sliding privacy doors and superior tech.

    But there’s at least a little nostalgia in bidding farewell to a cabin that, for many years, was billed as American’s most exclusive.

    According to recent reports, american was the last U.S. airline that claimed to offer a standalone, international first-class product.

    Across the global airline industry, many carriers sunset long-haul first-class years ago, choosing to instead offer more — and improved — business-class seats, which take up less space and are considered more profitable.

    For years, Delta Air Lines’ Delta One business-class suites have been its premier long-haul offering.

    United Airlines bid farewell to international first class in 2018 when it pivoted to Polaris business class.

    That left American’s Flagship First as a relic, of sorts, in the U.S. airline industry — and even on its own planes.

    In recent years, you could only find the cabin on two fleet types American operated: its Boeing 777-300ER, which offered eight of the pods up front in their own dedicated cabin.

    Plus, AA still (for now) offers Flagship First on its three-cabin Airbus A321T, which has been a fixture on lucrative coast-to-coast routes like Latest York to Los Angeles and San Francisco.

    But soon, it will be a thing of the past on both planes.

    American is retrofitting its larger 777s, ditching first-class in favor of 70 all-new Flagship Suites in business-class — along with the biggest premium economy cabin it’s ever offered.

    Related: This is now American Airlines' most premium plane: Here's what it's like on board.

    On domestic routes, the A321T will actually keep flying with Flagship First through March 28.

    But after that, AA will stop selling the Flagship First cabin on the A321T configuration, which is eventually going away as American flexes in its fresh A321XLR planes fully onto its top cross-country flights.

    In a lot of ways, American ditching Flagship First is a positive (and arguably overdue) transition for flyers.

    It’ll give passengers more lie-flat seats to pick from, whether they’re paying cash, using AAdvantage miles or using a systemwide upgrade.

    Also — while those Flagship First seats were really spacious and comfortable, many would say that American's new business-class product is a major upgrade from what it previously offered in that cabin.

    On some planes, that even includes extra-spacious Flagship Suites Preferred in the front and bulkhead rows of some planes, which offer a lot more space.

    Value check: Is it worth buying up to American Airlines' latest business-class Flagship Suite Preferred?

    Beyond the aircraft, American also prepares to still offer many of the same amenities for business-class that first-class passengers historically enjoyed.

    For instance, its Flagship business-class tickets get access to its premium lounges. Passengers traveling in Flagship Business and Flagship Business Plus on qualifying international, transcontinental and Hawaii routes will also be able to have a meal in its exclusive restaurant-style dining rooms in Dallas, Los Angeles and Miami.

    The experience is available on a space-available basis.

    So, in some ways, you could argue the end of Flagship First is more symbolic than anything.

    But for some AA loyalists, it's still a little bittersweet.

    TPG’s Clint Henderson is our resident Flagship First enthusiast, having flown the cabin on dozens of occasions.

    "The service in first class wasn't particularly differentiated, but I still liked a few of the special touches," he noted, pointing to the additional soup course and appetizer, along with a handful of elevated amenities.

    He especially appreciated the “La-Z-Boy-style” seats at the front of American’s 777s, which could lie flat or swivel and turn into an “office in the sky.”.

    “While these cabins are definitely showing their age,” Henderson added, “I’m sad to see it go.”.

    While Flagship First is technically going away as an official cabin on international service, the seats themselves won't disappear overnight.

    So far, American has only retrofitted one of its 20 Boeing 777-300ERs that feature the seats. That means a handful of jets with the old first-class seats will still be flying around well into 2027.

    According to recent reports, going forward, the former Flagship First seats on those planes will be marketed as business-class. They won’t come with the full first-class service, but you’ll still get the elevated seat.
